representative_fault: "Catching" the Rusher. Freezing feet while waiting for contact, destroying leverage and inviting a severe bull-rush.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Maintain continuous foot movement, sliding laterally or vertically to stay positioned strictly between the quarterback and the rusher.

representative_fault: "Catching". Standing straight up and waiting for the defensive end to make contact, giving away all leverage advantages.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Lower hips into an athletic quarter-squat on the first step. Maintain a square core to the imaginary defender so they stay centered between your legs as you run them horizontally.

representative_fault: "Clicking the Heels". Bringing feet close together during the kick slide, stopping lateral movement and destroying balance.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Drag the inside left foot to preserve a wide stance, keeping the edge rusher framed strictly between the knees on the outer arc.

representative_fault: "Diving at the Ankles". Throwing the body too low or too early, allowing the defender to easily step over the block or swat the back down without breaking stride.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Launch horizontally across the defender's frame, physically throwing your body sideways.

representative_fault: "False Stepping". Picking up the front foot and dropping it in place before advancing, which ruins the timing of the play and lets the defender strike first.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Exert maximum forward power to execute a devastating down block on an interior tackle or a base block to clear the edge.

representative_fault: "Gazing". Raising the eyes early to look for second-level linebackers before cleanly securing the down-lineman first.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Track the first power step directly through the crotch of the imaginary defender, framing the target tightly between both knees.

representative_fault: "Pop and Stop". Popping straight up out of the stance and freezing the feet the exact moment contact is made.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Maintain constant foot movement. Keep running your tracks with short, punchy steps to dictate the direction of the defender's momentum.

representative_fault: "Pop and Stop". Snapping the ball, landing initial contact, and freezing foot movement, allowing the rusher to effortlessly shed the block.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Sustain continuous 6-inch choppy steps into the turf until the pass is released - the feet never stop.

representative_fault: "Roll-Snapping". Rolling the shoulders forward over the toes during the snap, causing the center to lunge, lose balance, and get easily pulled down by the defender.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Fire out with a flat, driving posture - do not roll the shoulders forward over the toes.

representative_fault: "Sticking the Cleats". Planting the feet heavy upon first contact, leaving the guard vulnerable to a quick arm-over or spin move.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Shuffle laterally in low, active short steps, constantly resetting the base to mirror the defender until pass release.

representative_fault: "Tail-Skying". Pre-setting the stance with the hips too high, which forces the tackle to immediately step up instead of exploding forward.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Set up with the right hand down, right foot staggered back. Keep the head up, looking through the eyebrows at the target.

representative_fault: "Telegraphing the Cut". Lowering the pad level too early or staring at the defender's shins before launching, alerting them to brace or swim.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Aim your front shoulder directly at the thigh pad or knee line of the oncoming defender.

representative_fault: "Telegraphing". Placing too much weight heavily onto the down hand for a drive block, or leaning back on the heels when preparing to pull, tipping off the defense.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Assume a powerful 3-point stance with a slight left-foot-back stagger (toe-to-instep) to anchor and push forward-diagonal paths.

representative_fault: Bailing Hips Early. Pointing right toes entirely backward too early, removing inside post support and conceding an easy B-gap lane.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Keep feet wider than shoulder-width, sinking hips to keep the defender square in the middle of your vision and core frame.

representative_fault: Bending at the Waist. Reaching forward and bending at the waist completely shifts your weight off your anchor. This makes you highly susceptible to "push-pull" or "swim" moves, allowing the defender to effortlessly throw you face-first into the turf.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Secure the snap count and execute an aggressive "Angle Set" (a quick 45-degree lateral-forward step to the left) to instantly close the distance to the defender.

representative_fault: Chasing the Decoy. Aggressively kick-sliding outward to chase a defensive end who is purposely rushing wide to act as a decoy. This completely vacates the B-gap, leaving a massive, unblockable lane for a stunting linebacker to shoot through and violently hit the quarterback from the blindside.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: On the snap, take a controlled pass set backward and slightly outward, keeping the weight heavily distributed on the inside insteps to allow for instant redirection.

representative_fault: Chasing the Ghost. Drifting outside of your designated zone to chase a wide-rushing defensive end. In a slide protection, this entirely defeats the purpose of the scheme, tearing open a massive B-gap lane for an interior stunting tackle to hit the Quarterback immediately.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: On the snap, take a lateral "catch step" into the designated slide gap space to immediately seal the lane.

representative_fault: Chasing the Looper. Chasing a defensive lineman who purposefully loops outside completely vacates your assigned zone. This opens up an easy, direct interior lane for an inside stunting lineman to hit the Quarterback untouched.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: On the snap, take a lateral "catch step" to the left directly into the designated slide gap space.

representative_fault: Chest Forward. Letting chest drop forward over knees, stopping foot mobility and making the tackle top-heavy.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Work active, hot feet that continuously reset the base to absorb stabs, clubs, or bull rushes along the perimeter.

representative_fault: Climbing Too Quickly. Abandoning the double-team to climb to the second level too early leaves the defensive lineman un-secured, allowing them to split the block and instantly disrupt the backfield.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Secure the snap and take a hard, 45-degree "gallop step" directly into the hip of the defensive lineman.

representative_fault: Crossing the Feet. Crossing the trailing foot over the lead foot during the skip completely destroys your base. It guarantees you will trip over your own feet or immediately lose your balance and get knocked over upon hitting a defender.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: On the snap, open immediately with a short lateral slide step to the right.

representative_fault: Drifting Too Deep (Bowing). Taking too deep of a drop step and bowing backward into the backfield during the pull. This wastes critical milliseconds, ruins the geometry of the blocking scheme, and often leads to an immediate collision with the Quarterback or Running Back.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: On the snap, open immediately with a short, controlled lateral slide step to the right, ensuring you clear the depth of the guards and center.

representative_fault: Dropping Too Deep. Dropping too deep backward in the pass set abandons the line of scrimmage. This forces the pocket to shrink vertically, allowing the defensive line to easily compress the space around the quarterback and disrupt the throw.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: On the snap, set at a controlled 45-degree angle to the left, keeping a perfectly balanced weight distribution on the balls of the feet.

representative_fault: Ducking Head on Snap. Dropping the chin and breaking spine angle on the snap, losing visual tracking of the defender and surrendering leverage.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Keep the head up and preserve the spine angle on the snap - do not drop the chin or break the spine angle.

representative_fault: Elbow Flaring. Letting the elbows flare out on contact, which diminishes power and allows the defensive tackle to slide right off the block.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Explode both hands into the inside chest frame/armpits, clamping down on jersey cloth while keeping elbows tightly squeezed against the ribs.

representative_fault: Failing to Bring the Hips Through. Hitting the defender without rolling your hips through the contact results in a weak, top-heavy block. Relying entirely on upper-body strength guarantees you will lose leverage and get shed.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: On the snap, explode forward out of the stance with a powerful displacement step to instantly close the cushion.

representative_fault: False Stepping. Picking up the front foot and dropping it in place pre-snap, stalling the initial kick step and forcing the tackle to chase from behind.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Pop cleanly out of the stance, driving off the inside right foot into an explosive 45-degree vertical kick step with the left foot.

representative_fault: Flaring Elbows. Allowing elbows to swing outward, exposing the guard's own chest plate to easy control.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Explode the right hand out first as the primary strike into the chest, anchoring the left hand inside the opposite pectoral to stun momentum.

representative_fault: Getting Caught in "No Man's Land". Staring at one specific defender while a blitzer slips through the vacated adjacent gap destroys the integrity of the half-slide protection. You must protect the zone, not chase the man.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Secure the snap and take a diagonal 45-degree placeholder step toward the slide side.

representative_fault: Head Dropping. Dropping the eyes and head down on contact, causing the tackle to slide off the defender.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Deliver an upward-driving strike with the heels of the palms directly inside the chest plate, forcing the defender's momentum backward.

representative_fault: Leading with the Head. Launching head-first into a defender's knees, creating a dangerous risk for neck and concussive injuries.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Ensure the back or side of your shoulder connects with their legs to force the takedown.

representative_fault: Lunging & Over-Extending. Shifting weight onto the toes, which locks the knees, stops foot movement, and lets the rusher easily pull the guard forward.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Keep the feet pattering in micro-steps backward to absorb any power transition, anchoring the front-side pocket wall.

representative_fault: Lunging / Leaving the Feet Behind. Attempting to strike the defender by lunging aggressively with the upper body while the feet stop moving. This destroys your base, makes you extremely top-heavy, and allows a savvy edge defender to effortlessly pull you forward and throw you to the turf (the "pull-swim" or "judo" shed).
representative_ideal_execution_standard: On the snap, explode forward out of the stance with a powerful displacement step (often a lead or base step) to instantly erase the cushion between you and the defender.

representative_fault: Lunging Forward. Firing out of your stance and leaning forward allows the defender to easily use a swim or club move to bypass you instantly.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Secure the snap and execute a quick, vertical "Post Set" taking 1-to-2 short steps backward.

representative_fault: Narrow Base. Stepping too narrow on the second step, allowing the defender to easily push the guard sideways.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Drive the feet wide apart on parallel tracks so the imaginary defender's core remains strictly framed between the guard's thighs.

representative_fault: Opening the Gate. Bailing out too wide with the left foot and turning hips outward, opening a massive A-gap lane.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Execute a short, crisp angle set to the left, taking weight onto the inside leg (70/30 distribution) while keeping the base wide.

representative_fault: Over-Reaching. Lunging wildly on a reach block, causing the tackle to lose balance and drop to their knees.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Keep the hips square to the imaginary defender even when stepping at an angle, capturing and framing them perfectly between the knees.

representative_fault: Over-Setting (Opening the Gate). Kicking backward too deeply and turning your shoulders entirely toward the sideline too early. This "opens the gate," handing the elite edge rusher a direct, unimpeded path to execute an inside counter move (like a spin or rip) straight into the Quarterback's lap.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: On the snap, execute an explosive backward "kick step" with the outside (left) foot to instantly gain depth and widen the pocket.

representative_fault: Over-Stepping Flat. Taking a step that is too wide and flat, allowing an inside-shading defensive end to slice cleanly underneath into the gap.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Comfortably analyze the defensive front and seamlessly launch into lateral zone steps to the right or down blocks inside.

representative_fault: Over-Stepping Laterally. Taking a brace step wider than 6 inches creates a massive gap between you and the backside Guard, or causes your hips to turn sideways, ruining your anchor.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Immediately upon the snap, take a short, 6-inch lateral "brace step" with the foot closest to the slide direction.

representative_fault: Passive Steps. Taking a tentative, soft first step instead of an aggressive, ground-gaining lateral or drop step.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Utilize the uninhibited view of the edge to quickly read and execute wide-zone or reach blocks to seal the perimeter.

representative_fault: Pulling Too Deep. Looping backward into the backfield instead of running a tight line across the center's heels. A deep, looping path delays your arrival, allowing the unblocked defender to penetrate the backfield and blow up the play for a loss before you can execute the kick-out.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: On the snap, take an aggressive, perfectly flat "open step" to the right, pivoting exactly 90 degrees on the right foot to initiate the pull.

representative_fault: Pulling Too Deep. Looping backward into the backfield instead of running a tight line allows the unblocked defender to penetrate too deeply. This ruins the geometry of the play and results in a tackle for loss.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: On the snap, take an aggressive, perfectly flat "open step" to the right, pivoting exactly 90 degrees on the right foot.

representative_fault: Reaching / Clapping. Extending both hands prematurely with wide elbows, stripping away length and balance.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Deliver a stiff, independent left-hand strike to the chest plate to disrupt speed, keeping the right hand locked to catch inside counter moves.

representative_fault: Slowing the Timing. Allowing the purposefully bypassed defender to touch, chip, or slow you down in any way. You must clear the space instantly to allow your pulling teammate an unobstructed path to deliver the trap block.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Secure the snap and take a sharp, heavy "down block" step at an inside angle directly away from the trapped defender.

representative_fault: Splitting Apart. Stepping too shallow or failing to merge hip-to-hip leaves a physical seam between you and your blocking partner. This allows an aggressive, heavy defensive end to split the double team, breach the wall, and blow up the play in the backfield.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: On the snap, take a heavy lateral power step directly toward your teammate to instantly close any physical space between you.

representative_fault: Standing Up Straight. Popping upright out of the stance, raising pad level and erasing lateral redirection capabilities.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Slide the inside foot along the turf to preserve a shoulder-width-plus base, keeping the rusher centered over the outside knee.

representative_fault: Stepping Narrow or High. Coming out of the stance with a narrow base or popping completely upright surrenders all leverage, resulting in you being violently pushed backward directly into the Quarterback's or running back's path.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Secure the snap and fire out instantly with a low, explosive "power step" right through the crotch (midline) of the defender.

representative_fault: Turning the Hips and Running. Turning your hips and running like a sprinter blocks your vision of the second-level flow, makes it impossible to adjust to a linebacker's counter-movement, and leaves the backside open.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Secure the snap, push aggressively off the play-side foot, and take a lateral step backward with the backside foot to clear the line.

representative_fault: Waist Bending. Bending forward at the waist to reach for wide edge rushers instead of moving the feet to get there.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Maintain a push-replace foot rhythm, riding the rusher high and wide past the depth of the pocket while keeping feet churning.

representative_fault: Waist Bending. Bending over at the waist instead of hinging at the knees and hips, killing all leg-drive leverage.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Deliver high-knee, powerful driving steps, keeping your midsection directly aligned with the center mass of the imaginary threat.

representative_fault: Burying the Hand. Digging your fingertips deep into the mud and shifting your weight forward. This traps you in place, preventing you from sliding backward to protect the perimeter.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Lower your right hand to the ground, placing it lightly outside your right knee frame. Keep your left hand braced securely against your left thigh to complete your platform.

representative_fault: Deep Heel Stagger. Dropping the right foot 10+ inches back. A deep stagger in a gun alignment opens up your inside B-gap, inviting interior defensive tackles to shoot the gap for an instant sack.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Stagger your right foot back exactly 3 to 4 inches, aligning your right toe strictly with the mid-foot arch of your left shoe.

representative_fault: Deep Tackle Stagger. Dropping the right foot 12+ inches back like a tackle. A deep stagger locks up a guard's hips, making it nearly impossible to pull cleanly to the left or make a flat lateral block.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Stagger your right foot back exactly 4 to 6 inches, so your right toe aligns directly with the mid-foot or instep of your left shoe.

representative_fault: Fingertip Leaning. Placing forward pressure onto the ball. Leaning forward causes the ball to sail high or skip off the grass, leading to critical turnover fumbles.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Sink your hips deeply and shift your weight heavily backward onto your heels, balancing your weight at 40% forward / 60% backward. Your cleats must stay flat and glued to the turf so you do not fall forward while snapping.

representative_fault: Flaring Elbows. Letting your elbows flare out wide to the sides. Flared elbows open up your chest, allowing a defender to easily land an inside punch and control your frame.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Keep your hands up and open at chest level (ready to punch), or rest them lightly on your thighs with your elbows tucked securely into your ribs.

representative_fault: Head Dropping. Letting your chin drop to your chest while reaching down. If your eyes are locked onto your cleats, you will miss a late defensive blitz or an outside edge shift.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Lower your left hand to the turf into a clean 3-point stance, keeping the contact light. Brace your right hand tightly against your right thigh to complete your upper structural frame.

representative_fault: Heavy Hand Pressure. Placing heavy physical weight onto your down hand. If you lean forward, you cannot execute a flat lateral pull or a clean vertical pass set.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Drop your right hand down to the grass, placing only your fingertips on the turf with virtually zero weight on them. Tuck your left hand close to your left thigh in a ready state.

representative_fault: Heel Sitting. Letting your weight fall back entirely onto your heels with toes off the ground. This locks your ankles, making it impossible to launch forward if you need to execute a quick run-block.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Keep your hips sunk, but distribute your weight evenly at 40% forward / 60% backward. Your weight must stay entirely on the balls and heels of your feet, allowing you to move in any direction instantly.

representative_fault: Heel Sitting. Letting your weight fall back onto your heels. This locks your ankles, making it impossible to launch forward if you need to execute a quick run-block.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Keep your hips sunk, but distribute your weight evenly at 50% forward / 50% backward. Your weight must stay entirely on the balls of your feet, allowing you to move in any direction instantly.

representative_fault: High Hips. Standing up too vertical in a 3-point stance. High hips strip away your lower-body power, allowing defenders to easily push you into the quarterback's face.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Hold a rigid, half-squat frame. Keep your ankles and knees bent like springs, completely uncommitted to a direction until the ball is snapped.

representative_fault: Lazy Core. Failing to brace your abdominal muscles before the snap. A loose core causes your lower back to buckle the moment a physical defender makes contact.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Hold your loaded, half-squat posture. Keep your core fully locked and your knees bent, ready to instantly strike an inside rusher or slide out wide to protect the edge.

representative_fault: Leaning on the Ball. Placing too much upper-body weight directly onto the football. If the ball slips, you will collapse instantly into the dirt.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Sink your hips straight down into a deep squat, keeping your weight distributed evenly on the balls of both feet (50/50 balance). Do not lean heavily forward onto the ball, as this ruins your ability to handle a sudden defensive nose-guard rush.

representative_fault: Locked Front Knee. Failing to bend your front knee sufficiently when reaching down. This forces your back to hunch and locks up your legs.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Lower your right hand to the ground, placing it slightly outside your right knee frame. Keep your left hand braced securely against your left thigh to establish a rigid 3-point platform.

representative_fault: Narrow Base or Weak Stagger. Setting the stagger at only 4 inches. A shallow tackle stagger allows speed-rushers to instantly clip your outside shoulder before you can get depth in a kick-slide.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Take a wider 1.5-to-2-foot split from the Right Guard. Place your left foot forward and stagger your right foot back deeply exactly 10 to 12 inches, ensuring your right toe aligns directly behind your left heel to protect your outside edge.

representative_fault: Narrow Base. Setting your feet at a standard shoulder-width. A narrow base during a shotgun snap destroys your balance, causing you to tip forward the moment you snap the ball.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Approach the line and straddle the midline of the ball, spreading your feet 4 inches wider than shoulder-width to build an unyielding, broad anchor. Keep your spine flat, your chest proud, and your belt line perfectly square to the line of scrimmage, remaining completely balanced.

representative_fault: Over-Weighting the Hand. Putting 80% or more of your weight directly onto your down hand. This prevents you from reacting to a quick interior defensive stunt.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Drop your right hand cleanly to the turf into a traditional 3-point stance, placing your fingertips lightly on the ground. Tuck your left arm tightly to your left thigh, keeping the fingers relaxed but ready to engage.

representative_fault: Pre-Angling Hips. Turning your lower body outward toward the perimeter before the snap. This tips off the defense to an outside zone run or a slide protection schema.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Take a wide 12-to-18-inch split from the Center, placing your right foot forward. Keep your spine straight, your chest upright, and your shoulders squared completely to the defensive line.

representative_fault: Shallow Stagger. Setting a tight 4-inch stagger. A shallow stagger makes it impossible to get immediate depth in your pass sets, allowing speed-rushers to easily beat you around the edge.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Stagger your right foot back deeply exactly 12 inches, ensuring your right toe is positioned directly behind the heel line of your left shoe.

representative_fault: Spine Rounding. Letting your lower back arch or curve, which leaves you unable to generate upward explosive force.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Compress your lower joints fully. Keep your core braced and your mind locked on the snap cadence, ready to instantly explosive-drive or slide out wide.

representative_fault: Spine Rounding. Letting your lower back arch or curve. A rounded spine leaves you unable to absorb a heavy bull-rush, causing your pocket to collapse.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Compress your lower joints fully. Keep your core braced and your mind locked on the snap cadence, ready to instantly slide out wide.

representative_fault: Squatting Too High. Leaving your hips too high before the snap. Standing too upright strips away your natural leverage.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Lock in your low, loaded posture. Keep your spine perfectly flat and your core fully braced, ready to instantly drive off the line or transition into a pulling pattern.

representative_fault: Standing Upright. Failing to sink your hips. A high 2-point stance exposes your chest completely, allowing any edge rusher to easily drive you backward into the pocket.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Establish a wide 2.5-foot split from your guard, setting your left foot forward. Keep your chest upright and perfectly square to the line of scrimmage. Avoid leaning backward or standing too vertical, as this kills your natural leverage.

representative_fault: Turning Inward. Allowing your left hip and shoulder to angle toward the Center. This restricts your ability to pass-block an exterior rusher attacking your outside gap.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Align with a tight split next to the Center, setting your right foot forward. Keep your chest and shoulders squared completely to the defensive front line, preventing any pre-snap physical tipping of your assignment.

representative_fault: Unconscious Stagger. Allowing one foot to drift backward out of a habit. Any stagger from the Center creates an offset gap under your hips, causing quarterback-center exchange fumbles.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Approach the ball and straddle the midline of the football. Set your feet completely parallel (0-inch stagger / perfectly square), spaced slightly wider than shoulder-width apart to create a highly stable, square anchor.

representative_fault: "Flagging" the Ball. Carrying the ball loosely away from the body while running in space. This heavily exposes the ball to trailing defenders punching or stripping it from behind.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Hook the fingers over the front point, press the forearm along the seam, and clamp the back half of the football securely between the forearm and bicep.

representative_fault: "The Double-Clutch". Attempting to make a dynamic football move or break up-field before the ball is completely secured in the hands, leading to direct drops or immediate bobble-fumbles upon first contact.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Instantly secure the ball out of the snap exchange or handoff fake and transition it directly to the body, completely avoiding any "double-clutch" or premature up-field break before the ball is fully possessed.

representative_fault: Exposing the Breast. Carrying the football across the middle of the chest with a nose-up orientation. This allows a defender to punch it cleanly and violently out from the front.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Press the inner side of the football firmly against the rib cage with the nose tucked up beneath the armpit, completely locking the elbow to the torso to eliminate daylight.

representative_fault: Ball drops off the chest during the drop. Ball drifting off a consistent carriage position. (Ball Position needs ball tracking.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Football remains secure from snap reception through the drop — two-hand control until entering the throwing sequence.

representative_fault: Ball drops off the chest during the longer drop. Ball drifting off a consistent carriage position. (Ball Position needs ball tracking.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Maintain secure two-hand football carriage throughout the longer drop — the ball remains protected until the throwing motion begins.

representative_fault: Ball exposed or dropped to one hand during the fake/transition. (Ball Position needs ball tracking.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Maintain two-hand security during the fake and transition — the ball remains protected against the body until the QB commits to the throw.

representative_fault: Ball loose or away from the chest after the snap. (Ball Position needs ball tracking.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Maintain secure two-hand control after the pistol snap — the football stays protected against the chest before transitioning into throwing position.

representative_fault: Ball loose/low, elbows flared, or away from the body before the mesh. (Ball Position needs ball tracking.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Secure the football with two hands at chest level — throwing hand controls the back half, off-hand protects the front — ball tight to the body frame with elbows close until the mesh action begins.

representative_fault: Base too narrow/wide at the top of the deeper drop.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Maintain a stable athletic base after completing the drop — feet positioned to support immediate throwing mechanics.

representative_fault: Base too narrow/wide at the top of the drop for immediate throwing.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Maintain an athletic throwing base at the completion of the drop — feet positioned to support immediate throwing mechanics.

representative_fault: Base too narrow/wide at the top of the drop.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Maintain a balanced throwing base at the top of the drop — feet positioned for efficient release.

representative_fault: Base too narrow/wide for a quick release after the step.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Establish a balanced throwing base immediately after the step — feet underneath the body to support quick release mechanics.

representative_fault: Base too narrow/wide immediately after the step.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Establish a balanced throwing base immediately after the step — feet underneath the body to support efficient release mechanics.

representative_fault: Bouncing, high-stepping, or riding up on the toes instead of gliding. Base narrowing so the body leans and loses balance. Toes pointing backward. Crossing at a speed that costs control. Heavy heel contact or movement that disrupts timing.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Feet glide low to the ground throughout the drop — cleats cutting grass, staying in contact so a balanced throwing base is available immediately. Base stays wide enough to hold balance.

representative_fault: Bouncing, high-stepping, or riding up on the toes instead of gliding. Base narrowing so the body leans and loses balance. Toes pointing backward. Crossing at a speed that costs control. Heavy heel contact or wasted movement.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Feet glide low to the ground throughout the drop — cleats cutting grass, staying in contact so a balanced throwing base is available immediately. Base stays wide enough to hold balance.

representative_fault: Bouncing, high-stepping, or riding up on the toes instead of gliding. Base narrowing so the body leans and loses balance. Toes pointing backward. Crossing at a speed that costs control. Wasted steps or excessive vertical movement in the deeper drop.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Feet glide low to the ground throughout the longer drop — cleats cutting grass, staying in contact so a balanced throwing base is available immediately. Base stays wide enough to hold balance.

representative_fault: Drifting or off-balance first step disrupting throwing alignment.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Execute a controlled first step that maintains throwing rhythm while preserving balance and lower-body readiness — creating proper throwing alignment without drifting.

representative_fault: Drifts excessively deep or wrong depth relationship. (Absolute depth needs a scale reference.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Maintain proper pistol depth relationship from the center while reaching the required passing depth — creating space without drifting excessively deep.

representative_fault: Drifts off the shotgun relationship, hurting timing/lane. (Absolute depth needs a scale reference.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Maintain the appropriate shotgun relationship after the catch and one-step movement — preserving quick-game timing and throwing-lane integrity.

representative_fault: Elbows flare during the drop. Dropping to one hand on the ball. Arms stiff, or flailing/crossing the body’s midline, forcing the torso to overwork and sapping rotational energy.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Both hands stay securely on the ball throughout the drop. Arms and hands stay relaxed but controlled — not stiff, not so loose that the ball drifts and body position goes with it. Hands do not cross the body’s midline.

representative_fault: Elbows flare during the longer drop. Dropping to one hand on the ball. Arms stiff, or flailing/crossing the body’s midline, forcing the torso to overwork and sapping rotational energy.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Both hands stay securely on the ball throughout the drop. Arms and hands stay relaxed but controlled — not stiff, not so loose that the ball drifts and body position goes with it. Hands do not cross the body’s midline.

representative_fault: Extra gather steps or hesitation in the drop.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Maintain smooth timing from snap reception through the final step — no extra gather steps or hesitation.

representative_fault: Extra reset movement or disconnect between the catch and the drop.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Transition smoothly from shotgun reception into the five-step drop — catch and first movement connected without unnecessary reset movement.

representative_ideal_execution_standard: Receive the snap from under center — hands seated under the center, the ball delivered 'butt to gut' and immediately secured with both hands to the stomach/chest — with proper timing and rhythm, body balanced and prepared to execute the exchange.

representative_fault: Not clearing the midline, opening with the wrong foot, toes not squared parallel to the line, or crossing/choppy steps that stop momentum or drift off the path. (The track's aiming point depends on the run concept, which is not captured — reported, not judged.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Step off the midline ('step in the bucket') with the foot closest to the running back's side, squaring the toes parallel to the line of scrimmage into an athletic, basketball-defensive-stance base — efficient steps into and through the exchange with proper spacing, timing and balance, staying on the designed path. The toes align to the designated track for the called run (aiming point varies by concept).

representative_fault: Poor placement — wrong height/angle/firmness or misaligned with the RB's pocket. (Fully needs ball tracking + the RB — not measurable solo.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Place the football into the pocket created by the RB's arms and body — correct height, angle, and firmness, with nose/tip placement matching the running back's carry technique.

representative_fault: Pulls away early, releases to one hand, or exposes the ball before the RB secures it. (Ball position + possession need ball tracking + the RB.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Maintain two-hand control until the RB has secured possession — do not pull away early or expose the football during the exchange.

representative_fault: Staring Down the Target. Looking directly at the pitch man or shovel receiver early, alerting the linebackers and allowing them to jump the play.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Hold the attack trajectory until the defender physically commits to your chest.

representative_fault: Stops/stands up or loses balance instead of continuing the designed carry-out action. (Exchange-completion part needs the RB.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Complete the exchange with proper follow-through — maintain balance and continue the designed carry-out, fake, boot, or protection responsibility.

representative_fault: Wrong pistol depth relationship, breaking timing/spacing/blocking angles. (~3 yards is a recommendation, not a calibrated threshold; absolute depth needs a scale reference.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: From the pistol alignment (closer to the line, roughly 3 yards, upright to survey the defense), maintain the correct depth relationship so the exchange with the deeper-aligned tailback keeps its timing, spacing, and blocking angles.

representative_fault: Wrong shotgun depth relationship, breaking timing/spacing/blocking angles. (~5 yards is a recommendation, not a calibrated threshold; absolute depth needs a scale reference.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: From the shotgun alignment (roughly 5 yards behind the center), maintain the correct depth relationship to the line of scrimmage and the running back's path so timing, spacing, and blocking angles hold.

representative_fault: Ball drops to one hand or away from the chest, elbows flared, while navigating the pocket. (Ball Position needs ball tracking.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Maintain secure two-hand control of the football while navigating the pocket — ball tight to the chest with elbows close to the body until the throwing motion begins.

representative_fault: Ball drops to one hand or away from the torso while climbing. (Ball Position needs ball tracking.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Protect the football with two hands while climbing — ball remains tight to the torso until the throwing decision is made.

representative_fault: Ball exposed or dropped to one hand during the slide. (Ball Position needs ball tracking.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Keep two-hand control until ready to throw — the ball remains protected from pressure.

representative_fault: Ball exposed/one-handed while escaping — strip risk. (Ball Position needs ball tracking.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Secure the football with two hands while escaping — ball remains protected until the throwing decision.

representative_fault: Base collapses or feet leave the ground unnecessarily during the slide.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Maintain a stable base throughout the slide — feet remain connected to the ground.

representative_fault: Base collapses too narrow or spreads too wide during pocket movement.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Maintain an athletic throwing base with feet approximately shoulder-width apart throughout pocket movement — stable, without becoming too narrow or excessively wide.

representative_fault: Base narrows, posture breaks, or feet get out from under the body during the slide.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Slide efficiently left or right while maintaining base width, posture, and throwing readiness — feet remain underneath the body throughout the movement.

representative_fault: Base too narrow to absorb contact or redirect while climbing.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Maintain a functional throwing base during movement — feet separated enough to absorb contact and redirect.

representative_fault: Base too narrow/wide or unbalanced on recovery.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Return to a stable throwing base with appropriate width and balance.

representative_fault: Can't set a stable, aligned platform out of the climb.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Transition from movement into a stable throwing position with feet, hips, and shoulders aligned.

representative_fault: Can't transition from the escape into a throwing posture when needed.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Transition from escape movement into a throwing posture when required.

representative_fault: Carrying the Ball Low. Holding the ball down at your waist while sprinting out wide. Carrying the ball low lengthens your release time and increases the risk of a strip-fumble from a trailing defender.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Secure the ball tightly under your chin with both hands. Lean your shoulders forward and sprint horizontally toward the flat, using pure athletic speed to gain the edge on the defense.

representative_fault: Clicking Heels. Turning around so tightly on the open-gate pivot that your feet trip over each other. A sloppy first pivot slows your lateral velocity, letting an edge rusher hit you instantly.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Secure the snap cleanly. Take an immediate, wide open-gate pivot step at a 90-degree angle toward your rollout side, instantly clearing your frame from the center-exchange space.

representative_fault: Clicking Heels. Turning around so tightly that your feet trip over each other. A sloppy first pivot slows your lateral velocity, letting an edge rusher hit you instantly.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: On the snap, execute an immediate open-gate pivot (opening your hips 90 degrees directly toward your rollout path) and take a violent, deep escape stride sideways.

representative_fault: Crossing the feet or creating instability during the lateral slide.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Use controlled lateral steps with feet underneath the body — feet should not cross or create instability.

representative_fault: Crossing the feet, choppy/oversized steps, or unnecessary movement in the pocket.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Execute efficient pocket footwork using short, controlled steps without crossing the feet or creating unnecessary movement — maintaining proper stride length and rhythm while preparing to throw.

representative_fault: Drifting, bouncing, or excess lateral movement beyond what's needed to avoid pressure.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Move only as much as necessary to avoid pressure while maintaining throwing posture — avoid drifting, bouncing, or unnecessary lateral movement.

representative_fault: Drops the eyes, panics, or fails to adjust to pressure while keeping throwing posture. (Pressure recognition itself not pose-measurable — deferred.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Following the drop, maintain awareness of edge and interior pressure while keeping vision downfield — sense pressure without dropping the eyes and adjust movement while remaining in a throwing posture.

representative_fault: Escapes a clean pocket or misreads the break. (Perception/decision not pose-measurable — deferred.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Identify when pocket integrity has broken and determine the correct escape path.

representative_fault: Excessive forward/backward lean or collapsed posture while climbing.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Maintain athletic posture with chest up and spine stacked over the hips — avoid excessive leaning forward or backward.

representative_fault: Excessive lateral drift instead of a forward climb.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Climb forward through the pocket with minimal lateral drift, preserving throwing lanes and relationship with the offensive-line structure.

representative_fault: Eyes drop to the rush / ground while escaping. (Actual gaze not pose-measurable — deferred.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Keep eyes active downfield while escaping rather than focusing only on the rush.

representative_fault: Eyes drop to the rush/ground during movement. (Eye gaze/scanning not pose-measurable — deferred.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Maintain vision downfield throughout pocket movement while scanning defensive coverage and pressure — avoid dropping the eyes during movement.

representative_fault: Failing to Direct the Foot. Planting with your toe still pointed toward your deep drop track. This causes you to drift endlessly toward the sideline, completely shrinking your throwing window and running out of bounds.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: As you reach a depth of 6-7 yards deep in the backfield, slam your outside foot into the turf, instantly pointing your toe down a linear, downhill track toward the line of scrimmage. This foot serves as your steering rudder to stop your backward drift.

representative_fault: Failing to Direct the Foot. Planting with your toe still pointed toward your deep drop track. This causes you to drift endlessly toward the sideline, completely shrinking your throwing window.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: At the apex of your rollout, slam your trailing foot into the ground with the toe pulled up into sharp dorsiflexion. Instantly pivot and point your toe back downhill toward the line of scrimmage to gain control of your momentum.

representative_fault: Failing to Point the Toe. Planting with your foot still pointed wide of the target path. You will slip, blow out your base, or delay your break, resulting in an inaccurate, off-balance throw.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: As you clear the tackle box, slam your outside foot hard into the turf, instantly pointing your toe down a linear, downhill track toward the line of scrimmage. This compact step serves as your steering rudder to stop your backward drift.

representative_fault: Fails to climb from edge pressure, or overruns the pocket. (OL relationship implies linemen not in a solo clip.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Step vertically within the pocket to avoid edge pressure while maintaining throwing mechanics — controlled movement without overrunning protection.

representative_fault: False/unnecessary steps before moving to space.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Initiate movement toward available pocket space without unnecessary steps.

representative_fault: Finishes the climb off-balance or unable to continue into a throw/escape.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Complete the climb while maintaining balance and the ability to continue throwing or escaping.

representative_fault: Finishes the reset off-balance or not ready for continued action.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Finish the movement controlled and ready for continued action.

representative_fault: Finishes the slide off-balance or not ready for the next action.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: End the movement balanced and ready for the next action.

representative_fault: Head drops or bobs with the lower body. (Actual gaze not pose-measurable — deferred.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Keep eyes downfield while moving — head remains stable and independent from lower-body movement.

representative_fault: Head turns down/away from downfield during the slide. (Gaze not pose-measurable — deferred.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Maintain visual focus downfield while the body moves laterally.

representative_fault: Hips drift out from under the torso or over-open into the throw.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Maintain hips underneath the torso while moving and rotate efficiently into the throw without over-opening.

representative_fault: Hips left off-target or unable to rotate after reset.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Re-center the hips toward the target while maintaining rotational ability.

representative_fault: Hips lock up or shoulders lose throw-readiness during repositioning.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Allow the hips to rotate and reposition while keeping the shoulders ready to throw.

representative_fault: Inefficient acceleration or upright posture killing speed. (Ball control part needs ball tracking.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Accelerate efficiently with forward body lean while maintaining control of the football.

representative_fault: Late/unintentional movement or moving into pressure. (Pressure recognition itself not pose-measurable — deferred.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Recognize pressure location and identify available space before movement begins — movement is intentional and creates a cleaner throwing lane.

representative_fault: Long/uncontrolled steps or crossing the feet, losing balance.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Use short, controlled steps while maintaining a balanced base — feet remain underneath the body and avoid crossing.

representative_fault: Loses balance on the cut or no clear plant-foot transition.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Change direction without losing balance — the plant foot creates a controlled transition.

representative_fault: Loses body control finishing the escape. (Ball protection part needs ball tracking.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Complete the escape while maintaining control and protecting the football.

representative_fault: Loses target vision during the reset. (Gaze not pose-measurable — deferred.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Maintain or re-establish vision on the target throughout repositioning.

representative_fault: Needs extra gather steps to recover the throwing base after sliding.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Transition from the slide movement into a throwing base without extra gather steps.

representative_fault: Off-balance — head/shoulders/hips/feet out of alignment while moving. (Weight-centering is a proxy via hip-over-base.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Maintain body control with weight centered over the mid-foot — head, shoulders, hips, and feet remain aligned while climbing, sliding, or resetting.

representative_fault: Out-of-sequence (arm-first) throw after the reset.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Initiate the throw using the proper lower-body-to-upper-body sequence after the reset.

representative_fault: Over-leaning (losing vision/control) or too upright (losing speed). (Vision = gaze deferred; ball = proxy.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Maintain appropriate forward lean for acceleration without compromising vision or ball security.

representative_fault: Overstriding the Plant. Reaching too far forward to change direction out of the linear track. This locks up your hips and prevents you from getting your shoulders squared up to make an accurate throw.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Slip the ball out of the mesh late. Slam your outside foot down hard under your hips with the toe pulled up into sharp dorsiflexion. Instantly point your toe toward the perimeter to drive your body weight out of the linear track and onto a wide, looping rollout line.

representative_fault: Poor escape direction into leverage/traffic. (Decision needs defenders in frame — deferred.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Choose an efficient escape direction based on defensive leverage and available space.

representative_fault: Posture left collapsed/leaning after reset.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Restore neutral posture with chest up and shoulders stacked over the hips.

representative_fault: Reacts with upper-body lurching instead of a controlled first step.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Initiate movement with controlled footwork rather than excessive upper-body movement — the first step creates forward pocket space.

representative_fault: Rounding the Corner. Drifting too deep or running a lazy, wide circle into the backfield. Failing to point your foot and drive flat along the edge allows an unblocked defensive end to hunt you down for a loss.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Rip the ball out of the mesh at the last millisecond. Slam your outside foot hard into the turf, instantly pointing your toe and directing your final step down a wide, looping track toward the opposite edge. Hide the ball tightly against your back hip as you clear the edge.

representative_fault: Rushing the Pull. Sucking the ball back before the running back has fully closed their arms around the fake. A premature pull ruins the structural illusion, allowing the defense to immediately play the bootleg.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Secure the deep snap cleanly. Take a quick, short directional step toward the side of the incoming running back, prepping your hips for a high-speed diagonal crossing mesh.

representative_fault: Shoulders left misaligned with the target after reset.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Align the shoulders with the target after movement.

representative_fault: Shoulders tilt or hips drift out from under the body during the slide.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Maintain balanced posture while moving sideways — shoulders remain level and hips stay underneath the body.

representative_fault: Shoulders tilt/open early during movement, hurting the throw.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Keep shoulders level and square through movement before aligning the lead shoulder toward the throwing target — avoid opening early.

representative_fault: Slides toward pressure or drops the eyes. (Pressure recognition itself not pose-measurable — deferred.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Identify pressure direction and move away from the threat while maintaining vision downfield.

representative_fault: Slow or unbalanced reset — feet not set, hips unloaded, or shoulders not aligned after moving.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Re-establish a balanced throwing posture immediately after movement — feet underneath the body, hips loaded, and shoulders aligned toward the target.

representative_fault: Slow/inefficient hand separation delaying the throw. (Ball Position needs ball tracking.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Transition the football into proper throwing position with efficient hand separation.

representative_fault: Slow/unstable to set the throwing platform after movement — poor base, transfer, or alignment.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Establish an immediate throwing-ready position after movement with balanced feet, proper weight transfer, loaded hips, and shoulders aligned toward the target.

representative_fault: Standing Too Upright. Failing to bend at the waist during the linear handoff fake. Standing straight up exposes the empty ball to the linebackers, giving away the bootleg instantly.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Stick the ball deep into the stomach of the running back as they charge directly downhill. Keep your head and eyes locked into the mesh, shielding the ball with your upper torso to sell a heavy interior run play.

representative_fault: Staring Downfield. Keeping your eyes up and looking downfield during the mesh. If you don't commit your vision and head to the fake handoff, the linebackers will never bite on the run.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Seat the ball deeply into the running back's belly pocket with both hands. Ensure your head and eyes snap completely down into the fake mesh point, bending your waist slightly to shield the ball with your upper torso from the eyes of the linebackers.

representative_fault: The Floppy-Foot Slide. Planting with a loose, downward-pointing toe when trying to change direction. This causes you to slip on the grass and delays your escape to the perimeter.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Pull the ball back sharply. Slam your back foot hard into the dirt, pull your toe up sharply right before impact to anchor, and instantly direct your step out wide to the opposite flat. Keep your body compact to accelerate away from the unblocked defender.

representative_fault: Wasted/extra steps to replace the feet before throwing.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Replace the feet efficiently underneath the body after movement — no wasted steps before throwing.

representative_fault: Weak/off-balance first escape step — no separation.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Create separation from pressure with the first movement step while maintaining balance.

representative_fault: Weight left uneven/off-balance after reset. (Force is a proxy; balance/stance is the signal.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Restore balanced weight distribution between the feet to support throwing mechanics.

representative_fault: Base too narrow or too wide for a balanced exchange platform.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Feet approximately shoulder-width apart — roughly under the armpits — establishing a balanced athletic base that supports efficient snap reception and immediate movement after the exchange, with knees comfortably flexed and weight balanced on the balls of the feet.

representative_fault: Base too narrow or too wide for balanced shotgun reception.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Feet establish a balanced athletic base that supports clean shotgun reception and immediate movement after the catch.

representative_fault: Base too narrow/wide for balanced downhill movement.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Feet establish an athletic base supporting downhill movement immediately following snap reception.

representative_fault: Feet misaligned — poor balance during the catch/transition.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Feet remain aligned to support balance during the catch and efficient transition into the offensive play.

representative_fault: Feet square with no stagger, or the THROWING-side foot back instead of the non-throwing side — the back leg cannot load and the QB takes a false step forward to start the drop. Stagger too deep or too shallow to push off cleanly, or toe angle creating an unstable platform. (Judging which foot should be back requires the player's handedness.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Feet are staggered so the NON-THROWING-side foot sits slightly back — left foot back for a right-handed QB, right foot back for a left-handed QB. The stagger loads the back leg, lets the QB push off efficiently, and starts the drop without a false step forward. Feet stay roughly shoulder-width apart (about armpit width) with knees comfortably flexed and a stable toe-to-heel relationship and toe angle. NOTE: the stagger direction depends on the player's throwing hand — handedness must be supplied by the app before this can be judged; without it, report the observed stagger without scoring it.

representative_fault: Hands not seated under center, poor palm/finger relationship, or elbows flared — muffed/insecure snap. (Finger detail needs the hand model.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Bottom hand directly beneath the center with palm facing upward, top hand covering — fingers naturally spread and relaxed for a broad receiving target, wrists relaxed and elbows close to cushion the snap and immediately secure the football.

representative_fault: Hands off the window, stiff, or poor finger spread. (Finger detail needs the hand model.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Hands positioned comfortably in front of the torso at the anticipated snap location — fingers naturally spread and relaxed with elbows slightly flexed, creating a consistent receiving window that cushions the football into secure two-hand possession.

representative_fault: Hands too high/low/wide of the window, stiff wrists, or poor finger spread. (Finger detail needs the hand model.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Hands positioned comfortably in front of the torso at the expected snap location — fingers naturally spread with thumbs relaxed, elbows slightly flexed, and wrists soft to absorb the football cleanly into the body.

representative_fault: Head not neutral/level. (Actual eye focus not pose-measurable — deferred.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Head remains neutral while eyes focus on the expected snap location and maintain awareness of defensive alignment.

representative_fault: Head not neutral/level. (Actual eye tracking not pose-measurable — deferred.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Head remains neutral while eyes track the anticipated snap location and maintain awareness of defensive alignment.

representative_fault: Head tilted/dropped or chin not level. (Actual eye focus not pose-measurable — deferred.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Head remains neutral with the chin level — eyes maintain disciplined pre-snap focus while preserving proper body posture and awareness.

representative_fault: Hips off-square or not underneath the torso.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Hips remain square underneath the torso to maintain lower-body readiness immediately after the catch.

representative_fault: Hips rotated/off-square or not underneath the torso.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Hips remain square underneath the torso, allowing efficient force transfer immediately following the snap.

representative_fault: Hips unloaded/too high or spine rounded — not compact/balanced for the snap.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Hips remain loaded with the chest upright and spine neutral — the body remains compact and balanced while preparing to receive the snap.

representative_fault: Hips unloaded/too high or spine rounded — poor receiving posture.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Chest remains upright, hips loaded, and spine neutral while maintaining an athletic receiving posture.

representative_fault: Hips unloaded/too high or spine rounded — poor support for run/pass.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Maintain loaded hips, controlled chest, and neutral spine to support both downhill run action and passing mechanics.

representative_fault: Knees locked or over-bent — loses explosive readiness.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Knees remain slightly flexed, allowing explosive movement immediately after securing the football.

representative_fault: Knees locked straight or over-bent — loses athletic readiness.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Knees remain slightly flexed, creating an athletic posture that supports a stable exchange and efficient movement after possession.

representative_fault: Shoulders not square to the LOS.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Shoulders remain square to the line of scrimmage, allowing immediate transition into throwing, run, or mesh mechanics.

representative_fault: Shoulders tilted or not square to the LOS/center.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Shoulders remain level and square to the line of scrimmage and center, allowing a controlled snap exchange and efficient transition into the play.

representative_fault: Too shallow/deep behind center, forcing a reach or drift for the snap. (Absolute depth needs a scale reference.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Align at the prescribed depth behind the center while maintaining posture that allows the snap to enter the center of the receiving window without reaching or drifting.

representative_fault: Too shallow/deep behind center, hurting the window or timing. (Absolute depth needs a scale reference.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Align at the prescribed depth behind the center to ensure the football enters the optimal receiving window and preserves offensive timing.

representative_fault: Weight on the heels or rocking forward/backward, delaying movement. (Force is a proxy via ankle/COM position.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Weight centered through the mid-foot and balls of the feet, allowing explosive movement immediately after the snap without rocking forward or backward.

representative_fault: Weight on the heels or unnecessary body movement during reception. (Force is a proxy via ankle/COM position.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Weight remains balanced through the mid-foot and balls of the feet, allowing efficient reception without unnecessary body movement.

representative_fault: Weight on the heels — delays downhill movement. (Force is a proxy via ankle/COM position.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Weight remains balanced through the mid-foot and balls of the feet, supporting efficient reception and downhill movement.

representative_fault: Wrong stagger/toe angle — unstable reception or inefficient first movement.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Feet maintain proper stagger, toe angle, and alignment for balanced snap reception and efficient first movement.

representative_fault: Abrupt/unbalanced deceleration or hand finishes away from the target.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Decelerate naturally through the rotation — throwing hand finishes toward the target while maintaining balance.

representative_fault: Accuracy breaks down as velocity increases. (Velocity/accuracy/trajectory need ball tracking + a target — not measurable solo.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Maintain accuracy while generating increased velocity through rotational force.

representative_fault: Accuracy suffers from the reduced platform. (Accuracy/trajectory need ball tracking + a target — not measurable solo.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Deliver an accurate pass despite the reduced lower-body contribution.

representative_fault: All-arm throw — no ground-up energy transfer through the chain.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Generate force through the feet and transfer energy upward through the kinetic chain instead of relying only on the arm.

representative_fault: Arm fires before rotation (out of sequence) or elbow disconnects — arm-dominant, less velocity.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Arm accelerates after rotational sequencing begins — elbow stays connected to shoulder movement while the hand travels efficiently through the throw.

representative_fault: Arm mechanics break down off the reduced (airborne) platform.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Maintain efficient throwing mechanics despite the reduced platform.

representative_fault: Arm-dominant throw with hips not initiating, or hips out of control on the lower slot.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Lower body still initiates force production — hips rotate toward the target while maintaining control.

representative_fault: Ball misses the tight window or loses velocity. (Accuracy/velocity/window need ball tracking + a target — not measurable solo.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Deliver accurate throws through tighter throwing windows while maintaining velocity and control.

representative_fault: Base doesn't support the lower slot, or feet/hips/shoulders disconnect from the target line.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Athletic throwing base that supports a lower release angle — feet, hips, and shoulders remain connected toward the target.

representative_fault: Base too narrow/wide, stiff knees, or off-center weight — poor force transfer.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Stable throwing base with feet ~shoulder-width apart, knees flexed, hips lowered, athletic torso, weight centered to allow efficient force transfer.

representative_fault: Early release (before full transfer) or release point drifts as velocity rises — inconsistency. (Exact ball point needs ball tracking.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Ball releases after maximum energy transfer from the lower body through the torso; release stays consistent despite increased velocity.

representative_fault: Elbow drops/disconnects or the arm loops — inefficient, inconsistent path. (Ball position itself needs ball tracking.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Throwing arm follows an efficient overhand path — elbow connected to shoulder position, hand traveling behind and through the football.

representative_fault: Excessive side-sweep or looping in the arm path — inefficient, inconsistent sidearm.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Arm travels efficiently through a lower horizontal path without excessive side movement or looping.

representative_fault: Excessive sideways lean or falling away from the target — lost power and accuracy.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Transfer energy toward the target while avoiding excessive sideways lean or falling away from the throw.

representative_fault: Fingers off-center or no wrist snap — wobbly, uncontrolled rotation. (Finger detail needs the hand model; rotation needs ball tracking.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Fingers positioned behind the football to create controlled rotation; wrist snaps naturally through release while maintaining ball control.

representative_fault: Front shoulder opens early or shoulders tilt/dip through release — accuracy and power suffer.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Front shoulder stays directed toward the target during loading; shoulders rotate after hip initiation and remain level through release.

representative_fault: Hand cuts off early/across the body, or QB loses balance on the finish.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Throwing hand finishes toward the target; body decelerates naturally while maintaining balance and a recovery position.

representative_fault: Hard/uncontrolled landing or off-balance recovery — no readiness for continued movement.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Land under control with the knees absorbing force and the body prepared for continued movement.

representative_fault: Head drifts off the spine or destabilizes through the throw. (Actual eye gaze not pose-measurable — deferred.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Head remains stable over the spine; eyes stay focused on the target throughout the throwing sequence.

representative_fault: Hips and shoulders open together (no separation) — no stored torque, arm-dominant throw.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Create separation between hips and shoulders during loading — hips begin opening while shoulders remain closed to store rotational energy.

representative_fault: Inconsistent arm slot or elbow disconnected from shoulder — erratic sidearm release.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Maintain a consistent sidearm angle — elbow position stays connected to shoulder movement and supports the intended throwing lane.

representative_fault: Jump disrupts throwing posture or drifts off-line — lost control and accuracy.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Initiate controlled upward movement without disrupting throwing posture — the jump creates separation while maintaining directional control.

representative_fault: Legs flail or destabilize in the air, disrupting throwing alignment.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Maintain body awareness without ground contact — legs remain controlled to support throwing alignment.

representative_fault: Loses body position while trying to rotate in the air, or no rotation (all-arm airborne throw).
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Generate rotational force while airborne without losing body position.

representative_fault: Over- or under-adjusting the torso angle, or losing posture/balance creating the lane.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Adjust body angle to create the sidearm throwing lane while maintaining posture and balance.

representative_fault: Poor finger control at the altered angle — wobble or off-line rotation. (Finger detail needs the hand model; rotation needs ball tracking.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Fingers control the football's rotation and direction despite the altered arm angle.

representative_fault: Release point varies from throw to throw at the sidearm slot — inconsistency. (Exact ball point needs ball tracking.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Football releases from a consistent sidearm position with proper timing and trajectory.

representative_fault: Release too low/late/far forward, or short arm extension — accuracy and velocity drop. (Exact ball-release point needs ball tracking.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Ball releases at the optimal point above and slightly forward of the throwing shoulder, with arm extension and body alignment supporting accuracy.

representative_fault: Releases too early/late in the jump (e.g. on the way down) — lost power/accuracy. (Exact ball point needs ball tracking.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Release the football at the correct timing point during the jump sequence.

representative_fault: Shoulders drift off the target line while dropping to the lower slot.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Shoulders remain aligned with the target while supporting the lower arm slot.

representative_fault: Shoulders lead instead of hips, or hips slide laterally — broken sequence, lost torque.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Pelvis initiates rotation toward the target before the shoulders — hips rotate aggressively while maintaining posture and preventing lateral movement.

representative_fault: Shoulders open before hips (out of sequence) or hips slide laterally — lost power and accuracy.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Hips initiate the throwing sequence before the shoulders — pelvis rotates toward the target while maintaining balance and preventing lateral slide.

representative_fault: Shoulders open prematurely, spending the stored separation too early.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Front shoulder controls direction while the upper body stays connected to hip rotation; shoulders avoid opening prematurely.

representative_fault: Shoulders rotate off the target during the jump — accuracy suffers.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Shoulders remain directed toward the target through the jump and release.

representative_fault: Torso disconnected from hip rotation or spine collapses — energy leak between lower and upper body.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Torso transfers energy from the lower body into the upper body — chest follows hip rotation while maintaining spine alignment.

representative_fault: Torso/head destabilizes in the air or shoulders drift off target — airborne throw breaks down.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Maintain torso alignment while airborne — head stable and shoulders staying connected toward the target.

representative_fault: Unstable or misaligned posture before takeoff — compromises the whole airborne throw.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Create a stable throwing posture before leaving the ground — lower body loads while maintaining alignment and balance.

representative_fault: Weak/narrow base or torso not stacked — can't generate or transfer rotational force.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Strong rotational base — feet connected to the ground, knees loaded, hips athletic, torso stacked over the lower body.

representative_fault: Weight drifts or collapses, or force stays on the back leg — power leaks out of the throw.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Transfer force from the back leg through the hips into the target direction; the lead leg creates stability, preventing excessive drift or collapse.

representative_fault: Wrong velocity/trajectory/location for the route. (Ball outcome + accuracy need ball tracking + a target — not measurable solo.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Deliver the football with appropriate velocity, trajectory, and location based on the route and defensive situation.

representative_fault: "The Double-Clutch". Attempting to make a dynamic football move or turn up-field before the ball is completely secured in the hands, leading to direct drops or immediate bobble-fumbles upon first contact.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Instantly secure the catch in space and transition the ball directly to the body, completely avoiding any "double-clutch" or premature up-field turn before the ball is possessed.

representative_fault: "Catching" the Blitzer. Standing static at the line and waiting for the defender to make contact, allowing them to easily bull-rush the back straight into the quarterback.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Take an aggressive forward step toward the assigned protection gap to meet the blitzer inside the pocket perimeter.

representative_fault: Dropping the Head. Losing sight of the target right before contact, causing the fullback to completely miss the block.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Drive the palms hard directly into the defender's armpits, lifting upward to disrupt their center of gravity.

representative_fault: Lunging / Bending at the Waist. Diving forward with the head down, making it effortless for an athletic blitzer to execute a quick side-step or swim move.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Keep the chest up and eyes locked squarely on the blitzing defender's core.

representative_fault: Over-running the Angle. Charging directly at where the defender is pre-snap rather than tracking their movement, causing a total miss if the defender scrapes inside.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Take a lateral or diagonal departure step to strictly track the target's inside shoulder on an inside-out angle.

representative_fault: Pop and Stop. Landing a heavy initial collision but instantly stopping all foot movement, which lets the defender bounce off and make the tackle. Also: Narrow Track - bringing the feet close together right before contact, making the fullback top-heavy and easy to tip over.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Keep the feet wide and drive them with high-knee, powerful movements to roll the defender vertically back out of the hole.
