representative_fault: Soft Contact. Using an arm-swipe or hitting with the shoulder instead of shooting the hands, resulting in a weak block that the defender easily sheds.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Shoot the hands tightly inside the defender's frame, locking onto the jersey cloth to control the block.

representative_fault: BENDING AT THE WAIST - keeping the legs straight and simply leaning over. This ruins balance, alters eye level dramatically, and prevents running after the catch. THUMBS-UP MISTAKE - trying to catch a low ball with the thumbs together like a chest catch, forcing the hands upside down so the ball slips straight through onto the ground. (Hand inversion needs the Hand landmarker.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Track the downward trajectory and lower the entire body frame by bending at the knees and hips rather than folding at the waist. Drop the arms toward the grass with elbows tucked close to the torso, then invert the hands completely - pinky fingers pressed together, palms facing upward - creating a clean scoop to cradle the dipping ball.

representative_fault: BODY CATCHING - letting the ball travel all the way into the chest pads instead of extending the hands, so it bounces off hard plastic armour and results in drops or deflections. (Hand shape needs the Hand landmarker.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Hold a strong base with the eyes locked on the point of the ball. Shoot the arms forward away from the jersey to meet the ball early and maximise the catching radius, forming a tight symmetric diamond with thumbs and index fingers pressed together and palms turned outward to face the incoming ball.

representative_fault: Breaking stride or stuttering during the tuck, which surrenders the separation the route created.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Complete the tuck without breaking the vertical sprint into the end zone, preserving the separation the route created.

representative_fault: EARLY EYES - snapping the head up to look at the defence while the ball is still inches from the pinkies, causing it to slip through the arms onto the grass. On a low catch there is no margin: the eyes must stay down until the fingers close.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Keep the eyes hyper-focused on the hands and slide the inverted basket underneath the path of the ball, fingertips angled slightly upward right before impact, letting the ball land smoothly into the pinky basket while the fingers instantly curl around the leather.

representative_fault: Eyes leaving the ball before the tuck is complete - the head comes up to find defenders while the ball is still being secured, which is how a clean catch becomes a fumble. Also: no chin drop at all, so the catch is never visually confirmed.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Pull the ball tightly back into the ribcage, wrapping the arm completely over it for a four-point pressure hold. Instantly drop the chin to visually confirm the catch - nose to the tuck - before snapping the eyes upfield to look for defenders.

representative_fault: Eyes lifting off the basket before the fingers close. On a low-and-wide catch the hands are at their furthest from the head, so peripheral tracking is at its least reliable and the margin is smallest.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Slide the inverted hands underneath the dipping path of the ball, with the chin tucked to the catch-side shoulder and the eyes glued to the grass-level pinky basket as the ball settles in.

representative_fault: Head staying tilted up after the catch rather than following the ball down into the body, so the tuck is never visually confirmed. Also: landing stiff-legged without knee flexion, costing balance and the ability to run after the catch.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Pull the ball down violently to the chest as the feet return to the turf, the head snapping down to follow the ball's descent from the sky straight into the core, then immediately roll the body or shoulders over the ball to protect it from closing defenders.

representative_fault: Looking up to run before the ball is rolled securely into the abdomen. The low catch is the least secure of all four, so any early upfield glance during the roll-up is how the ball ends up on the grass.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Roll the hands and forearms upward toward the stomach, cradling the ball securely against the body frame so it cannot slip out. The eyes stay locked on the ball as it transitions from the grass line up into the stomach - do not look up to run yet.

representative_fault: PEEKING - letting the head drift back forward toward the end zone just before the ball drops into the bucket, so it hits the helmet or falls straight through the hands. THE PALMS-FORWARD BARRIER - facing the palms toward the line of scrimmage instead of up to the sky, creating a wall the ball bounces off rather than a basket it falls into.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The eyes track the nose of the ball dropping from the sky straight down into the open palms. The wrists stay completely loose and cushioned right before impact, letting the ball melt into the fingers without disrupting the running stride.

representative_fault: REACHING EARLY - running downfield with the arms extended to the sky for ten yards. This alerts the defender to play the arms, slows top sprint speed, and makes tracking the ball far harder. (Basket formation needs the Hand landmarker.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Sprint at top speed along the route track with a steady, bounce-free head. Keep the hands down and relaxed while running, extending the arms upward only at the absolute last second to keep the trailing defender blind, then raise the hands near collarbone or chin level with pinkies pressed together and palms open to the sky, forming a deep running basket.

representative_fault: REACHING WITH ONE HAND - extending only the leading arm, cutting the catching surface in half. (Hand shape needs the Hand landmarker.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Hold the running trajectory and snap the eyes toward the incoming ball, judging its lateral path while keeping stride length intact. Fire BOTH arms outward away from the torso into the lateral lane, torquing the upper chest slightly toward the ball without breaking the lower body's running line, and form a tight diamond out wide with thumbs and index fingers connected and palms squared to the side-angle trajectory.

representative_fault: Snapping the head forward before the ball is secured into the chest pocket, so the catch is completed blind.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Clamp the fingers around the ball the instant it settles into the hands, pulling it straight down into the pocket arm position while the head stays rotated over the shoulder and the eyes stay locked on the hands until the ball is safely into the chest - all without breaking the vertical sprint into the end zone.

representative_fault: THE BLIND PULL - tilting the head back down toward the turf before the hands secure the ball, resulting in a blind, clapping attempt at the apex. CLAPPING AT THE BALL - slapping the hands together from the sides; if the timing is off by a millisecond the palms hit the ball and knock it away.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Stare directly through the window created by the hands and pluck the ball out of the air at its highest possible point, fingers spread wide and thumbs facing each other right before impact, fingertips wrapping tightly around the tip and sides to halt its momentum mid-air.

representative_fault: THE EARLY CENTRE DROP - catching the ball diagonally but snapping the head back to the centre of the field before pulling it down, leading to a blind tuck and a high chance of dropping it on turf impact.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Pluck the ball out of the air at its highest possible lateral apex, staring directly through the diagonal window formed by the hands. The head must not drift back toward the centre of the body before the ball is secured.

representative_fault: THE EARLY LOOK - snapping the head up to look at an oncoming defender right before the ball hits the hands, causing a ricochet off the fingertips. THE STIFF-ARM CLANK - catching with locked-out elbows and hard palms; without joint elasticity a fast ball clanks off the hands. (Ball contact needs object detection.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Let the nose of the ball enter the centre of the diamond while the eyes stay hyper-focused on the leather. The elbows stay relaxed and flexible to give with the ball and absorb its force, with the fingertips - not the palms - clamping the panels.

representative_fault: The head returning to centre or upfield before the ball reaches the chest, completing the tuck blind - the most common way a spectacular high-and-wide catch becomes a drop on landing.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Pull the ball down violently across the chest, rolling the head diagonally downward to visually track the ball all the way from the high-outside quadrant into chest protection as the feet return to the turf.

representative_fault: The head snapping back downfield while the ball is still being swept across the body, so the rotational momentum of the sweep pulls the eyes off the leather and the ball is lost mid-transfer.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Sweep the ball back tightly across the body into the core ribcage, instantly snapping the chin down and across the torso to visually lock the ball into the tuck position before looking upfield.

representative_fault: The hips rotating with the chest, breaking the running line and costing stride.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Torque the upper chest toward the ball without breaking the lower body's running line, keeping stride length intact.

representative_fault: THE PERIPHERAL PEEK - trying to catch using only peripheral vision with the nose pointed straight downfield, which ruins hand-eye coordination and depth perception. THE STIFF LATERAL LOCKOUT - catching out wide with locked elbows, so the ball clanks off rigid fingertips.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Intercept the nose of the ball out wide in the centre of the diamond, elbows unlocked to absorb the high-velocity lateral momentum. The nose must be pointed exactly at the hands at the moment of impact - not tracking the ball peripherally.

representative_fault: THE UP-AND-OUT PULL - catching the ball low and wide but immediately pulling the head up and away to look at a defender, so the ball slips out of the pinkies during the lateral sweep. The longest, least secure transfer of any catch in the set.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Roll the hands and forearms upward and across the stomach, keeping the head down and rotated laterally. Watch the ball leave the lateral plane and physically touch the stomach before the eyes snap up to run.

representative_fault: TURNING PINKIES OUT - reaching up for a high ball with the pinkies together instead of the thumbs. This turns the palms away from the ball and makes a clean high catch impossible. (Hand orientation needs the Hand landmarker.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Track the high trajectory and time the jump or extension so the hands intercept the ball at the absolute apex of reach. Shoot both arms violently upward above the forehead with elbows slightly flexed, hands open wide with thumbs pressed tightly together and index fingers pointing up, creating an inverted triangle to look through.

representative_fault: TURNING PINKIES UP - reaching up and out with the pinkies together, which turns the palms completely away from the ball's path. THE OVERHEAD CLAP - slapping the hands together laterally from the sides instead of clamping the ball's incoming line. (Hand orientation needs the Hand landmarker.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Track the high, fading trajectory and time the jump or upper-body extension to meet the ball out wide at its highest point. Shoot both arms violently upward and outward on a 45-degree diagonal with elbows slightly flexed, hands open wide with thumbs locked together and index fingers pointing diagonally upward to form the overhead triangle.

representative_fault: WAIST-BENDING REACHES - keeping the legs straight and bending sideways at the waist, which destroys balance and pulls the eyes away from the ball. THUMBS-TOGETHER LOW CATCH - trying to scoop a low-lateral ball with the thumbs together, forcing the palms to face the ground. (Hand inversion needs the Hand landmarker.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Track the low, diving path and drop the entire body level by bending deeply at the knees and hips. Drop both arms diagonally downward toward the grass on the catch side with elbows tucked near the lower ribcage, inverting the hands out to the side - pinky fingers pressed tightly together, palms facing upward and outward - to form a secure under-scoop.

representative_fault: "Sticking the Cleat". Planting the foot flat and twisting the knee rather than rolling onto the inside instep, which can cause joint injuries or slips.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Plant the outside foot violently on its inside edge, driving all body weight straight into the turf.

representative_fault: Chopping Strides. Shortening the steps unnecessarily, which kills the back's top-end speed and lets pursuit players catch up.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Maintain a full, natural sprinting stride while approaching the designated turning point.

representative_fault: Elbow Flaring. Letting the football slip away from the ribs during the heavy plant, inviting a defender to strip it.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Clamp the ball tightly against the ribs to ensure it does not flare out during the heavy gravitational shift.

representative_fault: Hip Turning. Turning the entire chest and hips toward the sideline, slowing down forward speed and opening the back to edge hits.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Keep the shoulders completely square to the line of scrimmage throughout the entirety of the lateral glide.

representative_fault: Jumping Too High. Hopping vertically into the air rather than horizontally, which leaves the back suspended and helpless against waiting linebackers.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Plant hard with the foot opposite the desired direction to drive the body horizontally sideways.

representative_fault: Landing Flat. Falling flat onto the chest without driving the feet, causing the back's momentum to stop exactly where contact was made.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Maintain a wide driving base on the approach to generate maximum launching power.

representative_fault: Leaning Outward. Tilting the upper body away from the turn, which ruins balance and causes a wide, looping path.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Drop the inside shoulder slightly toward the direction of the cut to initiate a natural, inward body lean.

representative_fault: Narrow Landing. Landing with the feet close together, making it impossible to immediately accelerate post-cut.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Land with a wide, loaded base squarely on the balls of the feet.

representative_fault: Premature Extension. Reaching the ball out too early before passing the line of scrimmage, allowing a defender to easily punch it away.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Extend the ball safely over the line or marker at the absolute final microsecond, strictly after the line of scrimmage has been breached.

representative_fault: Tripping. Crossing the feet too tightly or low to the turf, causing the back to catch their own cleats and stumble.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Lift and forcefully drive the opposite leg across the body's midline to slide laterally into the adjacent gap.

representative_fault: "Clamping down" Early. Snapping the arms shut before the ball is completely seated in the midsection, causing fumbles or bobbles.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The instant the ball is seated, clamp both arms tightly over the ball to secure it against the midsection.

representative_fault: "Trailing Too Tight". Running directly behind or parallel to the quarterback, which destroys the pitch angle and allows one defender to play both threats.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Establish and maintain a strict alignment position exactly 4 yards outside and 1 yard behind the quarterback's tracking path.

representative_fault: Body Catching. Letting the spinning football hit the chest plate instead of catching it cleanly with extended hands.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Extend the hands away from the body with fingers spread wide and thumbs together to create a massive catching target.

representative_fault: Staring at the Exchange. Looking down at the quarterback's hands instead of keeping eyes up-field to read the defensive front and blocking keys.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Maintain a wide, stable pocket, allowing the quarterback to place the ball firmly into the stomach.

representative_fault: Turning the Head Early. Looking down-field to check for defenders before the ball is securely caught, leading to a dropped pitch or a muffed fumble.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Look the spinning football completely into the hands, physically tracking it with the eyes.

representative_fault: Unprepared Hands. Running with the arms swinging naturally instead of keeping them extended in a ready posture to catch the pitch.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Keep the hands up at chest level, palms facing the quarterback, forming a natural, permanent target framework.

representative_fault: "Dancing". Hesitating or taking multiple short, choppy steps at the snap instead of committing to a single, violent first step.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Operating from roughly 3 yards directly behind the shotgun QB, take a hard, single direct step forward with the lead foot.

representative_fault: "False Stepping". Dropping the back foot further backward or picking up the lead foot and placing it down in the exact same spot before moving forward, ruining the timing of the mesh.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Push violently off the back foot from a deep alignment (5 to 7 yards behind the QB), driving the lead foot forward 6 to 12 inches.

representative_fault: "False Stepping". Pivoting or dropping the rear foot further backward before launching forward, which delays the block and completely destroys the timing of the running back's path.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Explode forward out of the 3-point stance by physically rolling the body weight over the front knee.

representative_fault: Elbow Flaring. Flaring the elbows out wide on the initial burst, exposing the ribs and making it easier for inside blitzers to jar the ball loose.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Coordinate the first step with a sharp, aggressive backward drive of the elbows.

representative_fault: Popping the Top. Straightening the spine and standing tall on the first step, which raises the target area for defenders and kills forward momentum.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Keep the shoulders completely square to the line of scrimmage, leaning the upper body slightly forward to press the track downhill.

representative_fault: Rounding the Track. Taking a looping, curved step backward before crossing face, which alters the mesh timing and allows edge defenders to disrupt the exchange.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Drive the outside foot sharply across the body at a precise diagonal angle to travel horizontally across the formation.

representative_fault: Shooting Upright. Popping the head and chest straight up into the air on the first step, exposing the throat and breastplate to an easy wrecking block by the defender.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Elevate hands into a loaded strike position while keeping the chin tucked, spine flat, and shoulders lower than the oncoming linebacker's numbers.

representative_fault: Staring Down the Ball. Focusing entirely on the quarterback's hands instead of keeping peripheral eyes on the shifting defensive line and unblocking edge threats.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Keep the hands wide and clean to present an easy pocket for the quarterback while keeping peripheral vision on edge defenders.

representative_fault: Tail-Dropping. Lowering the hips further at the snap before moving forward, which causes the fullback to sit down and lose all explosive forward momentum.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Push violently off the inside ball of the staggered back foot, driving it forward into a short, punchy 6-to-12 inch step.

representative_fault: "Banana Routing". Rounding the vertical turn in a wide, looping circle, giving trail defenders time to recover.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Snap the hips vertically, aiming exactly 1 yard inside the sideline boundary.

representative_fault: "Drifting Down-field". Curving the route forward into the linebackers rather than running flat to the sideline, allowing under-coverage defenders to close the window.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Sprint directly outward toward the numbers on the sideline.

representative_fault: "Leaking Out Early". Slipping away before the pass rush develops, alerting the linebackers prematurely.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Engage or simulate a firm pass-block on an interior rusher for a full "one-thousand-one, one-thousand-two" count.

representative_fault: "Rounding the Break". Drifting through the inward turn instead of making a sharp cut, allowing the defender to maintain their cushion.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Cut back sharply at an inside 45-degree angle straight across the formation.

representative_fault: "Rounding Too Flat". Flattening out the route too early, bringing the back into the path of an unblocked edge rusher.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Execute a shallow, curved acceleration path strictly behind the line of scrimmage.

representative_fault: "Running Into Traffic". Running directly into an interior zone defender rather than searching out the open void.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Cleanly avoid all interior line wash without slowing momentum.

representative_fault: Cutting Too Shallow. Breaking backward into the line of scrimmage, clouding the throwing window with defensive linemen.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Ensure the reception phase happens at a strict depth of 3-4 yards past the line of scrimmage.

representative_fault: Losing Depth. Floating toward the line of scrimmage while running laterally, which narrows the throwing lane.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Maintain a constant depth of 2 to 3 yards deep in the backfield while hitting top speed.

representative_fault: Slowing Down at the Line. Reluctantly entering the LOS traffic, which completely disrupts the timing of the deep pass.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Burst directly out of the stance, tracking tightly through the open A or B-gap.

representative_fault: Staring Down the QB. Facing the quarterback with flat feet while waiting, which alerts defenders and stalls the forward track.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Keep the body hidden behind the defensive line while extending the hands to form a catch pocket.

representative_fault: Stepping Out of Bounds - running too close to the sideline on the turn, leaving no room for a clean drop-in pass.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Snap the turn aiming exactly 1 yard inside the sideline boundary, leaving room for a clean drop-in pass.

representative_fault: Turning for the Ball Late. Running with the head down and failing to look for the ball until hitting the boundary, causing drops.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Snap the head back toward the quarterback exactly after the third stride.

representative_fault: "Tail-Skying". Pre-setting the stance with the hips significantly higher than the shoulders, which forces the fullback to step straight up on the snap and lose all low-man leverage.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Load the hips low with the spine parallel to the ground or tilted slightly upward, keeping the knees deeply bent over the toes like loaded springs.

representative_fault: "Telegraphing". Shifting weight onto the toes when running a play to that side, or leaning back slightly on passing downs, giving away the play pre-snap.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Set feet strictly shoulder-width apart, keeping toes straight ahead with an optional, slight toe-to-instep stagger based on personal comfort.

representative_fault: Hands on Knees. Locking the elbows out and resting the upper-body weight heavily on the knees, which delays hand usage for pass protection or taking a clean handoff exchange.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Rest hands loosely on the upper thighs with elbows bent and tucked close to the ribs, ready to instantly form a ball pocket or strike a blitzer.

representative_fault: Heavy Hand Loading. Putting too much body weight onto the fingers of the down hand, causing the blocker to trip forward or lunge on their first step.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Rest minimal weight (roughly 20%) onto the fingertips of the down hand to avoid lunging on the snap.

representative_fault: "Lifting the Gate". Taking a step forward at the snap, which completely destroys the corner's cushion and allows a fast receiver to blow past them instantly.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: On the snap, take a concise 2-to-3 inch step backward without gaining or losing massive ground.

representative_fault: "Opening the Gate" to the Inside. Flipping your hips completely inward toward the hash marks too early, which blindingly exposes your deep outside boundary track.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Drop your outside foot back strictly at a 45-degree angle (slide-technique).

representative_fault: "Opening the Gate". Turning the back entirely to the sideline, allowing receivers to run easily into the deep hole behind the flat.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Keep your chest completely square to the line of scrimmage to read the passing lane.

representative_fault: "Reaching" / High Foot Lift. Lifting the knees high or reaching too far backward with the feet, which locks the knees and stops quick lateral redirection.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Push off the forward foot and reach backward with the toes of the back foot.

representative_fault: "Sinking the Hips Too Late". Letting a vertical receiver get within 3 yards of your cushion before you transition into a full sprint, allowing them to stack you vertically.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: If the receiver reaches top speed at 8 yards, immediately transition from a backpedal into a full hip-flip run.

representative_fault: "Sitting" on the Stem. Stopping the pedal around 7 yards because you anticipate a short route, making you highly vulnerable to an explosive double-move.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Use the compact arm swing to maintain maximum backward velocity until it is time to plant and break.

representative_fault: "Squatting" Too Early. Freezing on an underneath release, leaving the intermediate space behind you wide open for a dig or a post route.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Execute a precise lateral shuffle-weave or a slow tempo-pedal backward. Keep your base wide and stable.

representative_fault: "Squatting" Too Early. Freezing or moving downhill on an underneath route (like a 5-yard out), which allows a deeper vertical concept (like a corner or seam) to fly directly over your head.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Maintain a strict top-down cushion of 3 to 4 yards above the highest climbing vertical threat in your zone.

representative_fault: Allowing a Free Outside Release. Letting the receiver beat you cleanly down the sideline by stepping too narrow or failing to slide wide on the first step.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Take a quick lateral shuffle step to the outside to stay directly in the receiver's outside track.

representative_fault: Bailing Deep Immediately - turning and running deep at the snap, leaving a soft flat zone wide open for easy underneath completions.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Execute a balanced "motor-patter" or an immediate mirror step, keeping your feet low to the grass and moving rapidly in place.

representative_fault: Bailing Deep on the Snap. Dropping straight backward into a deep backpedal, which opens up the immediate flat zone for easy check-downs or out-routes.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Take an immediate lateral drop or heavy slide step toward the outside flat boundary.

representative_fault: Bailing Deep Too Fast. Running backward immediately at the snap, which leaves the short flat/curl zone wide open for quick completions.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Take an immediate lateral drop or heavy slide step toward your assigned zone track. Hold your depth line.

representative_fault: Bailing Hard Early. Flying backward at top speed without reading the play first, which leaves a massive void in the intermediate middle of the field.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Take low, smooth read steps backward.

representative_fault: Bailing to the Post. Over-retreating to protect the deep middle out of habit, which creates a massive cushion for the receiver on easy out-breaking or comeback concepts.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Use a controlled tempo backpedal or a tight kick-slide.

representative_fault: Bailing Too Fast. Flying backward at a full sprint immediately, which completely gives up the intermediate space and opens up easy 10-yard curl, hitch, or out routes.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: On the snap, push off the front foot directly into a controlled backward pedal.

representative_fault: Biting on Inside In-Breaks. Panicking and chasing a shallow inside route, leaving the deep outside completely open to a wheel or corner-route double-move.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Establish and rigidly maintain an outside-in trailing pocket.

representative_fault: Biting on Outside Fakes. Opening the inside hip and stepping out toward the sideline on a receiver's outside release fake, completely giving up the inside leverage.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Maintain an inside-out trailing relationship through the slide.

representative_fault: Biting on Play-Action. Flowing downhill aggressively into a run gap, allowing the tight end to slip behind you cleanly on a pop-pass route.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Take an assertive angle-approach step to lock in your pre-snap shade leverage on the tight end's framework.

representative_fault: Biting on Play-Action. Running forward on a run-fake, letting vertical seam routes stack behind your deep cushion for an easy touchdown.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: On the snap, execute a slow, balanced tempo-pedal straight backward to gain depth.

representative_fault: Chasing Crossers Out of the Zone. Turning to chase a receiver who is leaving your zone, which creates a massive void behind you for a stunting route.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Execute a patient lateral weave or tempo pedal, reading the triangle flow from the slot threat to the quarterback.

representative_fault: Cleat-Sticking. Planting the feet heavily into the turf during intermediate changes of direction, causing a total delay when matching an out-breaking route.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Force all intermediate tracks to the inside.

representative_fault: Cleat-Sticking. Planting your feet heavily into the turf during intermediate changes of direction, causing a total delay when matching an out-breaking route.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Maintain parallel foot tracks. Do not let your feet click together or narrow your stance.

representative_fault: Cleat-Sticking. Planting your feet heavily upon first contact, leaving you unable to match an intermediate cut or break.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Keep your base wide and keep your feet low to the turf, slide your cleats rather than lifting your feet high.

representative_fault: Clicking Heels. Letting the feet knock together during the pedal, ruining structural balance.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Slide the toes across the turf without gaining excessive deep yardage initially.

representative_fault: Clicking Heels. Shuffling or pedaling so erratically that the feet click together, leaving the corner off-balance.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Keep the backward steps fluid and low to the turf.

representative_fault: Drifting Prematurely. Drifting toward a hash mark too early without a clear threat, opening up a massive deep vertical void on the opposite side.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Maintain a strict top-down visual perspective, remaining the deepest player on the defensive side of the ball.

representative_fault: Dropping the Inside Foot. Stepping backward with the inside foot first, which opens the inside lane completely.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: At the snap, maintain inside posture by driving off the outside foot to slide laterally inside if the receiver tries to cross your face.

representative_fault: Early Trailing Disconnect. Allowing more than 2 yards of vertical space to open up during the initial trail phase, rendering your underneath tracking useless.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Ensure you remain slightly outside the receiver's path throughout the retreat.

representative_fault: Elbow Flaring. Raising the arms out wide like wings, which exposes the corner's chest and allows the receiver to clamp or swat the block easily.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Fire an aggressive outside-hand jam directly to the receiver's shoulder.

representative_fault: Eye Floating - looking up at the receiver's head, eyes, or shoulders, causing the nickel to bite heavily on head fakes.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Keep your weight centered over your core, remaining neutral until the receiver commits to a specific shoulder path.

representative_fault: Eye Floating. Looking up at the receiver's head, eyes, or shoulders, causing the corner to bite heavily on head fakes or upper-body jab steps.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Keep eyes locked firmly on the receiver's beltline/hips. Never look at the head or shoulders.

representative_fault: Eye Floating. Looking up at the receiver's head, eyes, or shoulders, causing you to bite heavily on head fakes or upper-body jab steps.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Keep your eyes locked on the receiver's hip/waist cylinder. Ignore head and upper body route fakes.

representative_fault: False Stepping Forward - taking a step forward at the snap, which surrenders a piece of the high cushion before the play develops.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Initiate a smooth read-and-drift pedal vertically backward to protect your deep middle third width.

representative_fault: False Stepping Forward. Taking a step forward out of a 10-yard stance, which defeats the entire purpose of playing deep cushion.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Glide out of the stance using low, sweeping backward steps.

representative_fault: Flat Feet - standing completely static at 10 yards and letting a high-speed vertical receiver erase the cushion completely before you start moving.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Take a slow, deliberate "read-step" backward (a spatial "tempo pedal" or "catch-step").

representative_fault: Flat Feet - standing static and letting a high-speed vertical receiver erase the cushion completely before you start moving.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Take an intentional angle-approach step to maintain your assigned shade leverage as you close the distance.

representative_fault: Flattening the Angle. Backpedaling flatly toward the sideline rather than deep, allowing vertical routes to stack you vertically from the inside.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Execute a deep "slide-backpedal" or weave pedal.

representative_fault: Giving Up the Inside Lane - turning your hips outward too early, conceding a soft inside release path across your face.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Take an assertive angle-approach step to lock in your pre-snap shade leverage on the tight end's framework.

representative_fault: Giving Up the Sideline. Getting crossed up or faked inside, giving up a clean vertical sideline release where the deep safety has the longest distance to travel.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Use the brace step to maintain a tight relationship strictly on the receiver's outside shoulder frame.

representative_fault: Guessing the Release. Lunging inside or outside before the receiver actually declares their cut, conceding an easy release on the opposite side.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Take an assertive angle-approach step to lock in your pre-snap shade leverage.

representative_fault: Guessing the Route. Turning the hips inside or outside prematurely before the receiver actually declares their cut, giving up an easy break on the opposite side.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Match the receiver's speed step-for-step during the retreat.

representative_fault: Heel Settling. Letting your weight shift entirely to your heels during the deep pedal, which locks your ankles and stops you from driving downhill on a comeback.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Keep eyes locked on the target's core frame, ready to drive downhill the microsecond their hips sink for a break.

representative_fault: High Knee Lift. Lifting the knees high off the ground during the deep retreat, which destabilizes balance and slows down lateral breaking ability.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Initiate a deep, high-cushion backpedal right at the snap.

representative_fault: Hips Flipping Sideways Early. Turning entirely sideways before the route declares, giving away your coverage width.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Keep your chest square to the line of scrimmage to read the overall flow of the passing concept.

representative_fault: Locking Eyes on the QB. Staring into the backfield while pedaling, causing the corner to completely lose spatial awareness of the wide receiver's intermediate crossing stem.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Keep your chest open to the inside field while retreating to read the quarterback's progression.

representative_fault: Locking Eyes on the QB. Staring into the backfield while pedaling, causing the safety to completely lose spatial awareness of climbing wideout stems.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Keep the feet moving continuously; never settle into a static position until the ball is thrown.

representative_fault: Losing Inside Frame. Drifting too far out toward the numbers, leaving the deep inside seam wide open for a vertical post route.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Maintain your inside alignment to force the receiver to run through your vision if they want to cross the field.

representative_fault: Losing Pad Level. Rising straight up out of the stance on the first step, which slows down backward velocity and ruins leverage.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Push directly off the forward foot to launch straight backward into a high-tempo pedal.

representative_fault: Losing the Shade. Taking an improper approach angle that allows the receiver to cross your face and establish easy leverage.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Take an intentional angle-approach step to maintain your assigned shade leverage as you close the distance.

representative_fault: Losing the Sideline Cushion. Pedaling in a straight vertical line and allowing a fast receiver to step on your toes and blow past your outside shoulder.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Begin the deep backpedal with an intentional, subtle drift toward the sideline.

representative_fault: Lunging at the Break. Throwing your torso forward when the receiver enters the catch window, causing you to slip or miss the trail.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Transition smoothly from your approach into a tight, trailing mirror-step once you enter the catch zone.

representative_fault: Lunging Punch - throwing the entire upper torso forward to punch a release, which shifts all weight past the toes and causes the safety to fall off-balance.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Take an assertive angle-approach step to lock in your pre-snap shade leverage on the tight end's framework.

representative_fault: Lunging Punch. Throwing the entire upper torso forward to punch an inside release, which shifts all weight past the toes and causes the corner to fall off-balance.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Punch with the inside hand directly into the receiver's chest plate.

representative_fault: Over-Sprinting Early. Immediately turning and running deep on the snap, which allows the receiver to easily break off an intermediate route into 10-12 yards of completely open space.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Initiate a smooth read-and-drift pedal vertically backward to protect your deep middle third width.

representative_fault: Premature Two-Hand Punch. Reaching out with both hands early, which robs the corner of their balance and allows the receiver to easily swipe the arms away.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Punch only when the receiver fully commits to a lane.

representative_fault: Reaching for the Ball Early. Turning your head to look for the deep ball before you have physically capped the receiver's shoulder, resulting in a pass interference or a separation touchdown.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Force the receiver to work inward toward your safety help while keeping them in your visual field.

representative_fault: Reaching with a Double-Hand Punch. Lunging forward with both hands, throwing away your balance and letting the receiver easily swipe past you.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Keep your weight centered over your core, remaining neutral until the receiver commits to a specific shoulder path.

representative_fault: Rising on the Snap - standing tall on the first step, which raises your pad level and strips away your ability to change direction quickly.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Take an assertive angle-approach step to lock in your pre-snap shade leverage.

representative_fault: Rising on the Snap. Standing tall on the first step, which raises your pad level and strips away your ability to change direction quickly.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Execute a balanced "motor-patter" or an immediate mirror step, keeping your feet low to the grass and moving rapidly in place.

representative_fault: Soft Boundary Touch. Delivering a weak strike that fails to disrupt the wideout's speed track, leaving the safety vulnerable over the top.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Deliver a physical strike into the receiver's frame to force them away from the seam.

representative_fault: Soft Boundary Touch. Delivering a weak strike that fails to disrupt the wideout's speed track, leaving the secondary vulnerable.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Sustain a wide, active base to react instantly to a throw or a block on perimeter run plays.

representative_fault: Soft Boundary Touch. Delivering a weak, single-arm swipe that fails to disrupt the wideout's vertical speed track, leaving the safety vulnerable over the top.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Deliver a physical, outside-arm strike (collision technique) directly into the receiver's chest plate.

representative_fault: Sprinting Out Early. Immediately turning and running deep on the snap, which allows the receiver to easily break off an intermediate route into 10-12 yards of completely open space.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Take a slow, deliberate "read-step" backward (a spatial "tempo pedal" or "catch-step").

representative_fault: Squatting Early - freezing on an underneath route (like a 5-yard out), which allows a deeper vertical concept to fly directly over your head.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Execute a patient lateral weave or tempo pedal, reading the triangle flow from the slot threat to the quarterback.

representative_fault: Squatting Early. Freezing on an underneath crosser and leaving the deep hole wide open for a dig or a post route behind them.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Maintain a top-down cushion of 4 to 5 yards above the highest climbing vertical threat in your assigned deep half.

representative_fault: Standing Tall. Straightening the spine, which raises the center of gravity and strips away all explosive downhill break power.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Maintain a forward body lean with the chest over the knees. Keep the chin tucked.

representative_fault: Staring at the QB. Peeking into the backfield early in man coverage, which causes you to completely miss the receiver's break point.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Keep eyes glued exclusively to the receiver's lower abdomen to track speed and depth metrics.

representative_fault: Sucking Inside. Getting drawn toward the middle of the field by an inside route, leaving the deep outside completely open to a wheel or vertical sideline route.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Keep your body positioned outside the inside hash line.

representative_fault: Sucking Outside. Over-reacting to an intermediate outside vertical stem, which opens a massive passing lane for a deep post or dig route inside.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Weave slightly inside during the pedal to maintain inside-out leverage advantage over the receiver's track.

representative_fault: Turning the Back to the Field. Flipping the hips fully sideways early, which creates a massive blind spot across the opposite deep seam.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Keep your chest square to the line of scrimmage to read the quarterback's shoulder alignment and drop-back length.

representative_fault: Turning the Back to the Sideline - opening the hips entirely outward, which ruins peripheral vision and stops you from seeing a secondary receiver crossing into the flat lane.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Take an immediate lateral drop or heavy slide step toward the outside flat boundary while keeping your chest strictly parallel to the line of scrimmage.

representative_fault: Turning the Back to the Sideline. Opening the hips entirely outward, which ruins peripheral vision and stops you from seeing a secondary receiver crossing into the flat lane.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Keep your chest strictly parallel to the line of scrimmage during the drop.

representative_fault: Turning the Hips Early. Turning the entire body to face the sideline on the snap, leaving you exposed to an easy inside cutback.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Keep the chest completely square to the line of scrimmage as the receiver makes contact.

representative_fault: "Bending at the Waist". Leaning the upper body too far forward over the knees, which shifts weight heavily onto the toes and traps the cornerback's hips, making it impossible to transition into a clean backpedal.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Sink the hips into an athletic quarter-squat. Keep the spine long and flat.

representative_fault: "Linebacker Creep". Setting up with a stance that is too wide and flat, with hands resting on the thighs, which locks up the feet and causes immediate delay against a quick pass route.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Place feet slightly wider than shoulder-width with an assertive toe-to-instep stagger, keeping the foot closest to the formation's core forward.

representative_fault: Bending at the Waist - leaning the upper body too far forward over the knees, which shifts weight heavily onto the toes.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Keep your knees deeply bent and your hips sunk low.

representative_fault: Flat Backside Foot. Letting the heel of the staggered back foot touch the grass flat, which deadens the leg muscle and creates an immediate delay on the snap.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Position feet strictly shoulder-width apart with a comfortable toe-to-instep stagger. Generally, place the inside foot forward to help look inside at the quarterback while keeping eyes on the receiver.

representative_fault: Hands on Knees. Resting hands on the thighs pre-snap, which completely exposes the chest to a wide receiver's immediate release jam.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Hands must be held loose and active strictly at chest height. Ensure hands are ready to punch or match a release.

representative_fault: Hands on Thighs. Resting hands on the thighs pre-snap, which completely slows down hand usage and initial movement.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Hold hands relaxed and active near the mid-torso. Keep hands completely clear of the thighs.

representative_fault: Heel Settling. Resting weight flatly on the heels, which prevents an explosive downhill or lateral launch.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Keep 60% of body weight balanced directly over the ball of the front foot.

representative_fault: Narrow Stance. Setting the feet too close together, which restricts lateral agility and causes tripping when breaking.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Set the feet slightly wider than shoulder-width apart with a minimal, comfortable toe-to-instep stagger.

representative_fault: Over-Staggering - setting the feet too far apart front-to-back, which traps the hips and prevents a fast lateral change of direction.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Place feet slightly wider than shoulder-width with an assertive toe-to-instep stagger, keeping the foot closest to the formation's core forward.

representative_fault: Over-Staggering. Setting the feet too far apart front-to-back, which traps the hips and prevents a fast lateral change of direction.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Feet are placed strictly at shoulder-width with a tight, disciplined toe-to-instep stagger to maximize multi-directional redirection speed.

representative_fault: Stance Too Deep or Tall. Setting up with a high chest, which reduces lateral acceleration and makes you vulnerable to an immediate jam or a quick slant.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Keep your knees deeply bent and your hips sunk low.

representative_fault: Static/Heavy Base. Locking the knees or resting weight heavily on the heels pre-snap, which creates a massive delay on the snap.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Distribute weight 50/50 on the balls of the feet.

representative_fault: Arriving on long strides rather than chopping the feet down, leaving the receiver committed and unable to adjust when the defender moves.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The final two steps before contact shorten and quicken, keeping the feet under the body so the receiver can react instantly if the defender moves laterally.

representative_fault: Arriving tall and only sinking at or after contact, so the defender gets underneath the receiver's pads and uprights him immediately.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The hips drop into a loaded athletic squat before contact, establishing low leverage so the receiver arrives underneath the defender rather than upright.

representative_fault: Base narrowing into a normal running stride as the receiver closes, so he arrives with no lateral leverage and gets moved off the block on contact.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The base stays wide throughout the approach - noticeably wider than a running stride - so the receiver keeps blocking leverage and can react laterally to the defender.

representative_fault: Dipping or ducking the head before contact - the receiver loses sight of the target and cannot adjust, and it is an unsafe way to take a collision. (Gaze itself is not pose-measurable - orientation only.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The head stays up with the eyes on the target through contact - the receiver sees what he is blocking rather than ducking his head into the collision.

representative_fault: Drifting off the tracking line during the approach, so the defender slips past inside or outside before contact is made. (Alignment to the defender needs them in frame - path consistency only.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The receiver tracks a consistent line onto the defender, staying square to them so they cannot slip past inside or outside before the hands fit.

representative_fault: Engaging with pads high or the torso upright, letting the defender get underneath and upright the receiver, who then loses the block immediately. (Relative pad level needs the defender in frame.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: At engagement the shoulders stay low - at or below the defender's pad level - with the torso angled forward so the receiver wins the leverage battle rather than being stood up.

representative_fault: Hands landing without hip extension behind them - an arms-only block with no ground force, which the defender sheds easily. Or the hips firing before the hands arrive, wasting the drive.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The hips extend hard as the hands make contact, driving ground force up through the torso and into the defender so the block has power behind it rather than just reach.

representative_fault: Knees straightening into contact, leaving the receiver stiff-legged with nothing to absorb the collision or drive through it; or collapsing so deep he cannot move his feet.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The knees hold a strong power angle - roughly 90 to 120 degrees - approaching and through impact, absorbing the collision and providing the platform to drive.

representative_fault: Over-running the block - arriving at full speed with no gather, so the receiver loses balance on contact and the defender sheds him easily. (Cushion distance needs the defender in frame.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The receiver closes the cushion under control - accelerating to eat up ground, then gathering before contact rather than running through the block at full speed.

representative_fault: Overstriding on the first step so the foot lands ahead of the body's mass, which kills the power base and leaves the receiver reaching rather than driving.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The first step is short, controlled and punchy, planting underneath the body's mass so power is available immediately rather than reaching out and losing the base.

representative_fault: Slow or short hand extension, so the receiver makes contact with his chest rather than his hands and has no control of the defender. (Hand placement on the defender needs them in frame; grip needs the Hand landmarker.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The hands shoot forward violently at engagement, extending fast into the defender's chest frame rather than arriving late or short.

representative_fault: Stopping the feet on contact and leaning on the defender, or standing up and narrowing the base after the hit - either way the block is lost within a second.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The feet keep driving after contact, moving the defender while the base stays wide and the knees stay bent - the block is sustained rather than a single hit.

representative_fault: A false step - a backward or sideways step before the first forward step - losing ground and time before the stem begins.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The first movement travels forward along the release heading. No backward or lateral step is taken before the drive begins - the receiver goes directly from the loaded stance into the first step.

representative_fault: Arms out of sync with the legs, swinging across the body's midline rather than driving front-to-back, or elbows flailing and locking so the arms add no drive.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Arms drive front-to-back in rhythm with the legs - opposite arm to opposite leg - at a consistent elbow angle, without swinging across the body.

representative_fault: Base staying wide through the whole 5 yards, costing efficiency and speed; or narrowing too early so the driving steps lose their power base.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The base starts wider through the driving first steps, then narrows progressively into a linear running track by the fifth yard as the receiver transitions from acceleration to running.

representative_fault: Drifting laterally off the stem heading across the 5 yards, changing the depth and angle at which the break occurs. (Whether the heading matches the called route needs the route to be declared.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The stem holds a straight, committed line across the 5 yards - the body travels on the intended heading without drifting laterally, so the route develops on time and the break happens where it should.

representative_fault: Excessive torso rotation during max-effort strides - the shoulders counter-rotating hard against the hips, wasting energy that should go into forward drive.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The torso stays quiet through the acceleration - shoulders and hips rotate only as much as the stride requires, so energy goes into forward drive rather than twisting.

representative_fault: Foot landing ahead of the hips at strike, creating a braking force that costs speed on every step - typically caused by overstriding out of the stance.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Each foot lands under or slightly behind the hips during the acceleration steps, so every strike drives the body forward instead of braking it.

representative_fault: Ground contact times staying flat or lengthening across the 5 yards - the receiver is not converting drive into speed, and each step absorbs rather than adds velocity.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Ground contact shortens progressively across the 5 yards - longer on the driving first steps, then quicker as speed builds and the receiver transitions to running.

representative_fault: Head bobbing, whipping or dropping through the drive, so the receiver cannot process the defender's leverage. (Gaze itself is not pose-measurable - orientation and stability only.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The head stays stable and level through the 5-yard drive, held steady enough to read the defender's leverage and cushion while the body accelerates.

representative_fault: Popping upright prematurely rather than rising gradually, losing the forward drive angle and cutting acceleration short.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Pads stay low out of the stance and rise smoothly and gradually across the 5 yards as speed builds, reaching upright running posture only once the acceleration phase is complete.

representative_fault: Standing too upright out of the stance, killing the drive angle; bending at the waist so the chest folds ahead of the hips; or holding the forward angle too long and failing to transition upfield.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The torso holds an aggressive forward drive angle through the early steps - roughly 45 to 60 degrees from vertical - then transitions smoothly upfield as speed builds. The angle comes from the whole body driving forward, not from bending at the waist.

representative_fault: Strides not expanding - staying short and choppy through the whole 5 yards; or opening up too early, overstriding out of the stance before speed supports it.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Stride length expands progressively across the first 5 yards - short and driving at Step 1, opening up as speed builds through Steps 4 and 5.

representative_fault: Velocity plateauing early in the 5 yards, or stalling between steps - the receiver reaches a speed and stops building rather than accelerating through the stem. (Absolute rate needs a scale reference.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Speed builds continuously across the first 5 yards - each step adds velocity, with no early plateau or stall in the acceleration.

representative_fault: Weight stalling or falling back behind the feet at any point in the 5 yards, so a step catches the body instead of driving it forward.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Weight moves continuously forward across the full 5 yards, staying ahead of the base of support so every step drives rather than catches.

representative_fault: A false step - a backward or sideways step before the first forward step - losing ground and time before the route begins.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The first movement travels forward along the release heading. No backward or lateral step is taken before the release begins - the receiver goes directly from the loaded stance into the first step.

representative_fault: Arms out of sync with the legs, arms crossing the body's midline rather than driving forward and back, or elbows flailing/locking so the arms add no drive.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Arms drive in rhythm with the legs - opposite arm to opposite leg - with the elbows held at a consistent working angle to add drive out of the stance.

representative_fault: Backward weight transfer before the roll-off, the whole foot leaving the ground flat rather than rolling through the toe, or excessive vertical rise instead of forward drive.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The receiver rolls off the front foot into the release - the heel lifts while the toe stays in contact, driving the body forward. The roll-off leads the forward travel rather than following it.

representative_fault: Base widening through the first steps, costing efficiency and drive; or narrowing so far the receiver crosses over and loses balance.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Feet stay under the body through the first steps - narrow enough to run efficiently, wide enough to stay balanced through the acceleration.

representative_fault: Drifting or rounding off the line rather than committing to a release angle. (Whether the angle matches the called release needs the route to be declared - not determinable from a solo clip.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The body travels on a consistent, committed path off the line, matching the angle the called release requires - inside or outside - without drifting or rounding.

representative_fault: First step drifting laterally off the release heading, widening the path and costing ground before the route develops.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The first step travels directly along the intended release heading, without lateral drift that costs ground or telegraphs the release direction.

representative_fault: Head whipping round or dropping during the release, or failing to transition from the ball to the release path. (Gaze itself is not pose-measurable - orientation only.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Head transitions from the inside snap cue to the release path and defensive target, turning under control without whipping or dropping.

representative_fault: Hips over-rotating off the release heading, widening the path and costing ground; or staying square when the release requires them to turn.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Hips stay driving toward the release heading through the first steps, opening only as far as the release path requires.

representative_fault: Long ground contact times, or the foot striking ahead of the body with backward velocity - braking on each step instead of driving.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Ground contact is short and driving - the foot strikes underneath the body and leaves quickly, adding speed rather than absorbing it.

representative_fault: Overstriding on the first step so the foot lands ahead of the body's mass and brakes rather than drives; or a step so short it fails to create separation.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The first step is short and driving rather than long and reaching - it establishes ground contact quickly and underneath the body so the second step can build speed.

representative_fault: Shoulders rotating away from the hips and the release path, disconnecting upper and lower body and telegraphing the release direction.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Shoulders stay connected to the hips and square to the release path, moving with the lower body rather than rotating independently of it.

representative_fault: Shoulders spiking upright on the first step rather than rising gradually, losing the forward drive angle and slowing acceleration.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Pads stay low out of the stance and rise gradually across the first steps as speed builds, rather than popping upright immediately.

representative_fault: Standing straight up out of the stance, killing acceleration; or bending at the waist so the chest folds forward ahead of the hips instead of the whole body leaning.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The torso leans forward through the initial acceleration, driving the body out of the stance. The lean comes from the whole body angled forward, not from bending at the waist.

representative_fault: Weight stalling or moving backward relative to the feet, so a step catches the body instead of driving it forward.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Weight moves continuously forward through the first three steps, staying ahead of the base of support so each step drives rather than catches.

representative_fault: A gather step or hesitation between the crossover and the burst, giving the defender time to recover and closing the outside lane the fake just opened.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The crossover foot plants and immediately pushes off into the outside lane - no gather step, no pause. The redirect is instantaneous, converting the fake straight into the escape.

representative_fault: A lazy crossover that never clears the midline, or one too slow to be believed - the defender does not bite and the outside lane never opens.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The push off the plant foot drives the rear foot sharply across the body's midline into the inside lane, committing hard enough to sell the inside release.

representative_fault: A rounded or gradual change of direction rather than a sharp reversal, so the diamond flattens into a curve and the defender recovers the ground the fake bought.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The plant foot drives explosively back toward the outside, the step reversing direction sharply enough to complete the diamond path and escape into the open lane.

representative_fault: A shoulder drifting outside the knee line at the plant, widening the frame and telegraphing the release direction before the crossover begins.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The shoulders stay tucked inside the width of the knees, keeping the frame compact so the defender cannot read which way the release is going.

representative_fault: A slow or gradual push-off out of the plant, so the receiver never clears the defender's level and stays inside their reach as the route develops. (Defender position is not in frame - path and acceleration only.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The plant foot drives explosively forward, accelerating the receiver past the defender's hip plane and clearing their level in one burst rather than easing into the route.

representative_fault: Arm pump dropping off during the push step, which signals to the defender that the receiver is about to stop rather than continuing inside.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The arm pump continues at full amplitude through the push step, sustaining the impression of a slant or post being run at full effort.

representative_fault: Arms staying passive during the crossover, or pumping late so the upper body lags the feet and the fake looks manufactured. (Finger and grip detail needs the Hand landmarker.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The arms pump hard toward the inside lane in time with the crossover step, mimicking a genuine release so the fake is complete from feet to hands.

representative_fault: Bursting through square-shouldered, leaving a full jersey surface exposed for a recovering defender to grab as the receiver passes.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The inside shoulder rolls away as the receiver bursts past, turning the chest off the defender and eliminating the jersey surface they could grab.

representative_fault: Chest rising or the shoulders falling behind the plant foot, so the weight sits back and the receiver cannot push cleanly back to the outside.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The shoulders stay over the toes as the plant foot lands, keeping the body stacked over the brake and ready to snap back toward the outside.

representative_fault: CLICK-BACK - dragging the driving foot instead of slamming it cleanly into the turf, which bleeds away the explosive power. Also: the foot sliding at contact rather than gripping.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The foot opposite the intended path slams cleanly into the turf with no slide, delivering full force to drive the body laterally and forward into the open lane.

representative_fault: Drifting through the hesitation rather than stopping cleanly, so there is no freeze for the defender to react to and the bait never lands.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The sliding foot plants firmly and the lateral movement stops dead for a fraction of a second, holding the wide base while the defender is frozen.

representative_fault: Drive leg failing to extend fully, leaving force in the ground; or the lead knee not driving through, so the first stride out of the plant is short.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The drive leg extends fully to deliver every bit of force, while the lead knee flexes and drives forward to take immediate ground into the lane.

representative_fault: Drive leg too straight at push-off, producing little ground force, so the attack step lacks the urgency needed to make the fake believable.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The drive leg holds an acute bend - roughly 110 to 130 degrees - producing maximum ground force to launch onto the diagonal.

representative_fault: Driving into the lane square-shouldered and upright, presenting a full chest for the defender to get hands on and re-route the release.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The leading shoulder dips into the direction of the release - getting skinny - so the receiver presents the smallest possible target as he attacks the lane.

representative_fault: DROPPING THE HANDS - letting the arms trail behind the body, leaving no protection against a recovering defender's arm bar or jersey pull. (Specific hand technique needs the Hand landmarker.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The trailing arm drives sharply past the shoulder plane with a swift chop, clearing the defender's frame as the receiver locks onto the vertical track.

representative_fault: DROPPING THE HANDS - letting the arms trail behind the body, leaving no protection against a recovering defender's arm bar or jersey pull. Also: an arm path that never clears the shoulder plane. (Specific hand technique needs the Hand landmarker.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The trailing arm drives violently past the shoulder plane - swipe, chop or club-rip - shattering the defender's reach as the receiver clears vertically.

representative_fault: Escaping square-shouldered, leaving a full jersey surface exposed for a trailing defender to grab or arm-bar.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The trailing shoulder rolls inward and away as the receiver clears, eliminating the jersey surface a recovering defender could grab.

representative_fault: Feet shuffling, creeping or resetting during the read, which breaks the freeze and tells the defender a move is coming.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The feet stay planted wide and parallel through the read - completely still, holding the base while the defender is frozen.

representative_fault: Front knee straightening or losing its bend during the kickstep, so no energy is stored and the escape has to be generated from a standing start.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The front knee holds an acute bend - roughly 100 to 120 degrees - absorbing force and storing elastic energy for the escape rather than straightening under the load.

representative_fault: Hands dropping as the receiver concentrates on the footwork, leaving him with no answer if the defender reaches out mid-slide. (Finger and grip detail needs the Hand landmarker.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The hands stay up at lower chest height and relaxed through the slide, ready to react the instant a jam comes.

representative_fault: Hands dropping below the hips during the kickstep, leaving the receiver unable to counter the jam. (Finger and grip detail needs the Hand landmarker.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Hands stay active and up around lower chest height, ready to fight the defender's hands, never dropping below the hips.

representative_fault: Hands dropping or going passive during the hesitation, leaving the receiver with nothing ready when the jam arrives. (Finger and grip detail needs the Hand landmarker.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The hands stay up at chest level and active through the read, ready to strike the moment the defender's hands come.

representative_fault: Hands hanging away from the frame or extended early, giving the defender something to grab and leaving nothing loaded for the escape. (Finger and grip detail needs the Hand landmarker.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The hands retract tight to the lower chest and ribcage in a compact ready position, loaded to swipe or punch as the escape begins.

representative_fault: Hands hanging loose or away from the frame during the pause, giving the defender something to grab and leaving nothing loaded for the strike. (Finger and grip detail needs the Hand landmarker.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The hands retract tight to the lower ribcage into a compact ready position, loaded to strike as soon as contact comes.

representative_fault: Hands staying low or arriving late, so the receiver has nothing ready when the defender's hands come. (Finger and grip detail needs the Hand landmarker.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The hands come up quickly to chest height into a tight, relaxed ready position as the feet land - loaded to strike but not tense.

representative_fault: Hands staying passive or low through the plant, leaving the receiver defenceless at the exact moment the defender is most likely to reach. (Specific hand technique needs the Hand landmarker.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The hands come up fast into an aggressive strike position as the plant lands, ready to meet the defender if they reach out at the transition.

representative_fault: Hands staying passive through the drive, leaving the defender free to land a clean jam on a receiver who is already committed to a direction. (Specific hand technique needs the Hand landmarker.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The hands fire up and forward as the plant lands - striking, clearing or bypassing the defender's jam in the same instant the body drives.

representative_fault: Hands staying wide or low at the plant, leaving the chest unprotected at the exact moment a defender who bought the fake is arriving. (Finger and grip detail needs the Hand landmarker.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The outside hand crosses over the chest frame at the plant, shielding the body against any late contact from a defender closing on the fake.

representative_fault: Head coming round slowly after the breakout, so the receiver is late finding the quarterback and the ball on a route designed to come out quickly. (Gaze and ball location are not pose-measurable.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The head snaps round toward the sideline and upfield the instant the breakout fires, re-establishing vision to locate the quarterback and track the football.

representative_fault: Head dipping toward the feet as the body loads at the plant, losing sight of the defender at the moment the release is about to start. (Gaze itself is not pose-measurable - orientation only.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The head stays level through the plant, holding a neutral forward line rather than dropping to look at the feet as the body loads.

representative_fault: Head dipping toward the feet or lifting off the defender's midsection line during the kickstep. (Gaze itself is not pose-measurable, and the defender is not in frame - orientation only.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The head stays level and locked forward toward the defender's belt line - reading the hips rather than the hands or the feet.

representative_fault: Head dropping to watch the feet during the slide, or turning upfield early and telegraphing the vertical release. (Gaze itself is not pose-measurable - orientation only.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The head stays level and locked on the defender's belt line throughout the slide, tracking them laterally without dropping to the feet.

representative_fault: Head dropping to watch the feet during the split, losing sight of the defender at the moment the read has to happen. (Gaze itself is not pose-measurable - orientation only.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The head stays level and locked on the defender's belt line through the split, with no downward dip toward the feet as the body resets.

representative_fault: Head starting to turn back outside before the plant lands, giving the defender an early warning and letting them jump the breakout. (Gaze itself is not pose-measurable - orientation only.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The head holds the inside fake alignment right up to the exact plant frame, then prepares to snap back - the deception is maintained to the last possible instant.

representative_fault: Head staying still or turning too slowly during the crossover, leaving the fake incomplete. (Gaze itself is not pose-measurable - orientation only.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The head snaps sharply toward the inside lane in time with the crossover, adding the final piece of the fake - the defender reads the eyes as well as the feet.

representative_fault: Head staying turned toward the fake after the escape, or turning back slowly, so the receiver loses track of the defender and is late finding the ball. (Gaze and ball location are not pose-measurable.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The head snaps back upfield to align with the route, re-establishing vision quickly so the receiver can track the cushion and find the ball.
