representative_fault: Head staying turned toward the release side after the escape, or coming round slowly, so the receiver is late reading coverage and late finding the ball. (Gaze and ball location are not pose-measurable.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The head comes round to track straight upfield, re-establishing vision quickly so the receiver can read coverage depth and locate the football.

representative_fault: Head still turned toward the slide side after the burst, or coming round slowly, so the receiver is late reading coverage and late finding the ball. (Gaze and ball location are not pose-measurable.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The head comes fully round to track upfield along the route, re-establishing vision quickly so the receiver can process cushion and locate the ball.

representative_fault: Head turning back toward the outside before the plant, breaking the deception early and letting the defender sit on the breakout. (Gaze itself is not pose-measurable - orientation only.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The head stays locked straight down the inside path through the push step, holding the deception right up until the plant.

representative_fault: Head turning before the plant (telegraphing the direction) or well after it (leaving the receiver driving blind into the lane). (Gaze itself is not pose-measurable - orientation only.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The head snaps toward the chosen attack path as the plant fires, committing the whole body to the direction in one motion.

representative_fault: Head turning upfield during the hesitation, tipping the vertical release before the read is complete. (Gaze and the defender's reaction are not pose-measurable.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The head stays locked forward on the defender through the pause, reading whether their hips open or freeze before the receiver commits to the vertical.

representative_fault: Head turning well before the plant (telegraphing the vertical) or lagging behind it, so the body commits before the receiver has picked up the lane. (Gaze itself is not pose-measurable - orientation only.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The head begins turning upfield toward the release lane as the plant lands, leading the body into the vertical transition.

representative_fault: Hips never finishing their rotation, leaving the receiver running at an angle across the field rather than vertically, which costs separation and distorts the route.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The hips rotate fully to point straight downfield, locking the receiver onto the vertical track so the route can develop at full speed.

representative_fault: Hips opening slowly or lagging behind the plant, so the drive has no rotational force behind it and the receiver pushes sideways instead of exploding through the lane.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The hips turn and open violently toward the chosen lane the instant the plant foot hits, converting the loaded base into directional drive.

representative_fault: Hips opening slowly or only partway, so the receiver drifts out of the cut rather than exploding, and the separation the fake created is given straight back.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The hips snap violently open toward the sideline, flipping the body off the inside track and onto the outside release in one decisive rotation.

representative_fault: Hips rising during the hesitation, unloading the base - the receiver then has to re-sink before moving, which costs the advantage the split created.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The hips stay low through the read, preserving the loaded position so the receiver can explode in whichever direction the defender opens.

representative_fault: Hips rising during the kickstep, unloading the legs and costing the elastic energy needed to escape.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Hips stay sunk low through the kickstep, holding the loaded height established in the stance with no upward rise.

representative_fault: Hips rising during the pause, unloading the spring - the receiver then has to sink again before transitioning, which gives the defender time to recover.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The hips stay low and loaded through the hesitation, holding the compressed position so the forward transition can fire without a reset.

representative_fault: Hips rising through the push step, so the receiver looks like he is preparing to stop rather than sprinting a route - the defender reads the cut coming.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The hips stay dropped and fully committed to the inside trajectory, holding the low sprinting position that makes the fake believable.

representative_fault: Hips rotating during the slide, opening the receiver to the defender and tipping the release; or the hips rising and falling, which turns a glide into a hop.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The hips travel horizontally at a constant height with no rotation, staying square to the defender so the slide gives away nothing about the eventual release.

representative_fault: Hips rotating slowly or incompletely, so the receiver drifts sideways out of the release instead of driving upfield, losing ground on the route stem.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The hips rotate sharply from the inside fake toward the sideline and upfield, converting the lateral momentum of the crossover into vertical drive up the field.

representative_fault: Hips rotating slowly or only partway, leaving the receiver running at an angle across the field rather than vertically - the slide's advantage is lost in the transition.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The hips flip sharply from the lateral slide orientation to point straight upfield, locking the receiver onto the vertical track in a single decisive rotation.

representative_fault: Hips staying high or drifting forward past the plant foot, so the spring never loads and the escape has no power behind it.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The hips drop and shift slightly back over the plant foot, compressing like a spring so the escape can launch in any direction.

representative_fault: Hips staying level or rising at the plant instead of sinking, so nothing loads and the transition to vertical has no power behind it.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The hips sink further at the plant, loading the lower body so the lateral energy can be redirected into forward acceleration.

representative_fault: Hips staying square while only the feet cross over - the fake is not sold, and the defender reads the outside release immediately.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The hips drive hard laterally across the defender's face, rotating toward the inside lane so the whole body sells the fake rather than just the feet.

representative_fault: Hips staying square while only the feet take the diagonal, so the fake is not sold and a disciplined defender reads the outside release immediately.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The hips accelerate along the 45 degree path and rotate fully onto the inside diagonal, committing the whole body to the fake from the first step.

representative_fault: Knees extending during the slide, which pops the body upward into a hop; or collapsing so deep the receiver cannot cover ground laterally.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Both knees hold a consistent bend - roughly 120 to 140 degrees - through the slide, producing a smooth lateral glide with no upward bounce.

representative_fault: Knees staying at their kickstep angle or straightening at the plant, so the receiver is upright and committed rather than loaded and able to go either way.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Both knees bend deeper at the plant, dropping the receiver into a loaded crouch that can launch in any direction.

representative_fault: Knees staying too straight to load the split, or weight settling back onto the heels so the receiver cannot push off cleanly.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Both knees bend deep into an athletic squat - roughly 90 to 110 degrees - with weight balanced evenly over the balls of the feet, ready to drive in any direction.

representative_fault: Knees straightening during the hesitation, so the springs unload and the drive-off has to start from scratch.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Both knees hold their deep flexion through the read - loaded springs, ready to extend the instant the defender commits.

representative_fault: Knees straightening or wobbling during the hesitation, so the receiver loses balance on the wide base or unloads the legs before the transition.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Both knees stay deep and stable through the pause, absorbing the lateral momentum and holding balance on the wide base.

representative_fault: Landing tall and sinking afterwards, so there is a moment where the receiver is upright and unloaded - the split buys no advantage if the hips arrive late.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The hips drop the instant the feet land, lowering the centre of gravity immediately so the base is established and loaded in a single motion.

representative_fault: Lead knee staying square or trailing the foot across, so the lower body does not commit and the fake reads as a feint rather than a release.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The lead knee flexes and drives aggressively inward across the body, pointing along the inside fake path to sell the release direction.

representative_fault: LEANING EARLY - tilting the head or shoulders toward the intended release during the micro-pause, which completely tips off the true direction and wastes the freeze.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Quiet shoulders - no tilt, no rotation, no lean. The upper body gives away nothing while the receiver reads which way the defender is going.

representative_fault: LEANING EARLY - tilting the head or shoulders toward the intended vertical route during the micro-pause, which completely tips off the true direction. Also: leaning back rather than forward, so no vertical threat is presented.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The torso tilts slightly forward over the toes to threaten an immediate vertical launch from the side lane, while the shoulders stay quiet and give nothing away.

representative_fault: LEAVING THE CHEST EXPOSED - turning back outside with the chest wide open, which invites a trailing defender to land a heavy recovery punch and push the receiver off his path.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The inside shoulder rolls away from the defender as the receiver breaks out, turning the chest off them and eliminating the jersey surface they could grab.

representative_fault: LOOKING AT THE DEFENDER - peeking at the DB instead of locking down the 45 degree track, which breaks the illusion before it is established. (Gaze itself is not pose-measurable - orientation only.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The head locks straight down the 45 degree inside path from the first step, selling the route rather than checking on the defender.

representative_fault: Low knee drive and an incomplete trailing-leg extension, so the first strides out of the release are short and the receiver takes too long to reach full speed.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The outside knee drives high and the trailing leg extends fully at push-off, taking ground upfield immediately rather than shuffling out of the release.

representative_fault: Low knee drive on the push step, betraying that the receiver is not truly accelerating and is already preparing to plant.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The back knee drives high and hard on the push step, simulating full sprint acceleration so nothing about the movement suggests a fake.

representative_fault: Low knee drive out of the breakout, so the first strides are short and the receiver takes too long to convert the cut into separation.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The outside knee drives high toward the sideline and upfield, taking immediate ground and building instant separation out of the cut.

representative_fault: Low knee drive out of the burst, so the first strides are short and shuffling and the receiver takes too long to reach full speed after the transition.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The lead knee drives high out of the transition, taking immediate ground upfield and accelerating the receiver toward top speed.

representative_fault: Low knee drive out of the escape, so the first strides are short and shuffling and the receiver takes too long to reach full speed.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The outside knee drives high through the escape strides, building linear speed immediately and creating separation from the defender.

representative_fault: No hand action at the breakout, or an arm path that never crosses the shoulder line, leaving a recovering defender's hands attached through the escape. (Specific hand technique needs the Hand landmarker.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The trailing arm executes a heavy downward chop past the shoulder line, clearing the defender's arms as the receiver breaks back to the outside.

representative_fault: No hand action at the escape, or an arm path that never clears the shoulder plane, leaving the defender's hands attached through the release. (Specific hand technique needs the Hand landmarker.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The trailing arm drives sharply past the shoulder plane - swipe, chop or swim - clearing the defender's hands as the body escapes outside.

representative_fault: OVER-SPLITTING - landing far too wide, which locks up the hips so the receiver cannot push off to change direction. Also: feet leaving the ground at different times rather than together, or landing staggered instead of parallel.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Both feet leave the ground at the same instant, the back foot snapping forward and the front foot back, landing parallel and wider than shoulder width to establish a balanced, uncommitted base.

representative_fault: Passive or low-amplitude arm action that does not match a real sprint, leaving the upper body out of step with the feet and weakening the fake.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The arms pump hard at chest height in a genuine sprint-start rhythm, matching what a real slant release would look like.

representative_fault: Planting on a stiff, straight leg, which cannot absorb the lateral force - the receiver slides through the plant or has to take a recovery step before going vertical.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The planting knee bends sharply - roughly 90 to 110 degrees - absorbing the lateral energy of the slide and converting it into straight-line power.

representative_fault: Planting on a stiff, straight leg, which cannot absorb the momentum or store energy - the receiver slides through the cut and the breakout has no power.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The planting knee flexes deep - roughly 90 to 110 degrees - creating a spring-loaded platform to drive back out toward the sideline.

representative_fault: Planting with a braking action that kills momentum, or a base widening beyond shoulder width so the receiver has to gather before escaping.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The front foot plants firmly with no braking, and the feet stay tight within the body's frame - at or inside shoulder width - so the escape can fire in either direction.

representative_fault: POP-UP BRAKING - letting the chest and hips rise when trying to stop. Without sinking the hips to absorb the momentum, the receiver slides or stumbles instead of cutting cleanly.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The hips drop sharply and shift slightly back at the plant, sinking to absorb the forward momentum and load the push back outside.

representative_fault: Running through the release square-shouldered, presenting a full chest for the defender to get hands on and re-route the receiver.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The inside shoulder rolls away from the defender - getting skinny - so the receiver presents the narrowest possible surface as he clears the contact window.

representative_fault: RUSHING THE READ - turning the head toward the intended path before the defender has declared, or skipping the read entirely and committing blind. (Gaze and the defender's reaction are not pose-measurable.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The head stays locked on the defender's midsection through the read, processing whether they freeze, lean, or slide before the receiver commits.

representative_fault: Shoulders lagging behind the feet or staying upright rather than driving low onto the diagonal, so the upper body never commits to the lie.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The shoulders rotate fully square to the 45 degree line with the torso driving low and forward, exactly as they would on a genuine slant.

representative_fault: Shoulders rotating away from the hips during the slide, disconnecting the upper body and signalling the release direction before the receiver has committed.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The shoulders stay wide, level and square to the defender, moving with the hips rather than rotating independently of them.

representative_fault: Shoulders rotating during the split, which tips the release direction before the receiver has even read the defender.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The shoulders stay perfectly square to the defender through the split, with the torso leaning slightly forward over the knees to shield the chest.

representative_fault: Shoulders rotating open during the kickstep and telegraphing the release, or the torso leaning back away from the defender instead of staying over the toes.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The torso holds a slight forward lean over the toes while the shoulders stay square to the defender, giving away nothing about the intended release direction.

representative_fault: Shoulders staying level through the crossover, so the upper body never sells the inside move and the defender stays square to the outside release.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The inside shoulder dips hard and the torso leans into the inside lane, committing the upper body to the fake so the defender has to honour it.

representative_fault: SLAMMING INTO THE DB - releasing directly into the defender's body instead of taking an angled, tight path past their hip. The aim is to clear their frame, not initiate a collision. Also: drifting wide of the track and losing ground. (Defender position is not in frame - path tightness only.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The escape step drives straight upfield on a tight angled path past the defender's hip, clearing their level entirely rather than drifting wide or running into them.

representative_fault: SOFT CLEAT PLANT - failing to slam the outside foot into the turf with force. A soft plant results in a slow, sluggish transition from horizontal to vertical, and the foot drifts rather than gripping.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The outside foot slams aggressively into the turf and grips, arresting all lateral momentum in one contact so it can be converted straight into forward drive.

representative_fault: SOFT FIRST STEP - taking a tentative, short step instead of an aggressive 45 degree launch. The receiver must look like he is sprinting a slant from step one. Also: losing ground backward before the step fires.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The back foot fires outward on a sharp 45 degree diagonal toward the inside lane, launching straight onto the diagonal track with no ground given up first.

representative_fault: Staying square and upright through the plant, presenting a full chest just as the receiver commits and giving the defender a clean target to re-route.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The inside shoulder dips at the plant, lowering the chest profile and getting skinny against the defender's leverage as the transition begins.

representative_fault: Stepping backward and losing ground to the defender, or kicking the rear foot wide of the front foot rather than directly behind it, which widens the base and slows the escape.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The rear foot kicks directly behind the front foot to load the release, without giving up ground backward. The step loads the body rather than retreating from the line.

representative_fault: THE BUNNY HOP - jumping or leaping sideways instead of sliding. Hopping lifts both feet too high off the ground, leaving the receiver completely vulnerable if a defender jams him mid-air. Also: feet crossing rather than staying parallel.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The receiver pushes off the front foot and slides the back foot sideways, feet staying wide and parallel and low to the ground, moving laterally to bypass the jam rather than through it.

representative_fault: The plant foot sliding or drifting at contact rather than gripping, so the momentum is not arrested and the receiver needs extra steps to change direction.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: On the third step the outside foot slams into the turf along the 45 degree line and grips, acting as a violent brake that kills the inside momentum in one contact.

representative_fault: The second step drifting off the 45 degree line or shortening, so the diagonal track bends and the defender reads that the inside move is not real.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The opposite foot drives down the exact same 45 degree line as the first step, taking real ground inside so the fake reads as a committed route.

representative_fault: Torso rising toward upright during the push step, which tips that a plant is coming rather than a continued sprint inside.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The torso stays low and forward in an aggressive sprinting posture through the push step, matching what a genuine slant would look like.

representative_fault: A gather or recovery step between the plant and the first driving step, or the step drifting off the new line - either way the separation the cut created is handed straight back.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The inside foot drives immediately along the new route line with no drift, no gather step and no wasted movement between the plant and the acceleration.

representative_fault: A gather step between the plant and the drive out, or a high, short first step - either way the stored energy is wasted and the defender recovers the separation the stop created.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The receiver pushes explosively off the instep of the plant foot into a low, linear first step - the anchor converts straight into acceleration with nothing wasted.

representative_fault: Arm mechanics changing during the load step - shortening, tightening or breaking rhythm - which gives the defender a visual cue that the break is imminent.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The arm pump continues exactly as it was through the stem - unchanged amplitude and rhythm, so nothing about the upper body signals the load.

representative_fault: Arm pump shortening or slowing during the stem, a visual tell that the receiver is about to break down.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The arms pump violently through the stem at full sprint amplitude, driving the vertical push and giving no hint the break is coming.

representative_fault: Arm pump shortening or slowing during the stem, an early visual tell that the receiver is about to break.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The arms pump at full amplitude past the ribcage throughout the stem, driving the sprint and giving no indication a break is coming.

representative_fault: Arms flying wide at the plant, slowing the rotation and costing time in the break - and often unbalancing the receiver as he exits. (Finger and grip detail needs the Hand landmarker.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The arms stay tucked tight to the chest through the plant, keeping the frame compact so the body rotates as fast as possible into the new direction.

representative_fault: Arms staying compact or pumping weakly out of the break, so the upper body adds nothing to rebuilding speed from a dead stop - where it matters most.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The arms fire back into a violent punch-like pump the instant the drive out begins, mechanically restoring sprint momentum from a standing stop.

representative_fault: Arms staying tucked or pumping weakly out of the cut, so the upper body contributes nothing to rebuilding speed on the new line.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The arms fire back into a violent forward pump the moment the cut is made, mechanically driving the receiver back up to sprinting speed.

representative_fault: Arms staying wide through the bait, slowing the rotation and costing the receiver time in the break. (Finger and grip detail needs the Hand landmarker.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The arms pull in tight to the body as the turn begins, tightening the frame so the receiver can rotate faster into the break.

representative_fault: Arms still swinging wide through the breakdown, throwing the receiver off balance at exactly the moment he needs to be stable. (Finger and grip detail needs the Hand landmarker.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The violent sprint pump compacts into a tight position near the chest, quieting the arms so they do not fight the deceleration or unbalance the body.

representative_fault: BAILING OFF-TRACK - drifting wide toward the sideline or inside toward the middle right off the snap. Scurrying off the track ruins the spacing of the concept and runs the receiver straight into zone defenders.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Explode off the ball with a violent, low pad-level release to clear the press defender's hands and establish a strict linear track down the hashes or the seam lane, then transition smoothly into top-end sprint posture with stride lengths opening to maximum expansion, chin tucked and core locked on the track.

representative_fault: BANANA STEMMING - curving the path inward before making the actual break. A rounded line lets an inside-shade defender stay in front of the receiver the whole way. (Absolute depth needs a scale reference and the called depth.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Sprint hard downfield for 10-12 yards (12-15 on the deeper variation), pushing the vertical stem straight through the defender's outside shoulder to force them to protect the deep outside lane. One step before the break, drop the weight subtly into the hips and prepare to transfer laterally - without any choppy or gathering steps.

representative_fault: BANANA STEMMING - curving the path inward before making the actual break. A rounded line lets an inside-shade defender stay in front of the receiver the whole way. (Absolute depth needs a scale reference and the declared route.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Run an ultra-aggressive vertical stem for 12-15 yards, pushing directly at the defender's midsection to freeze their leverage and force a deep backpedal respecting the post or go. At break depth, violently drop the weight into the hips and chop the cleats heavily through a 3-step breakdown to absorb the extra momentum the longer stem has built.

representative_fault: BANANA STEMMING - curving the path inward before the actual break, letting an inside-shade defender stay in front the whole way. CHOPPING FEET - gathering or stutter-stepping before the break; a slant relies entirely on pure unmitigated speed, and chopping ruins the separation.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Fire off the line hard for 3 direct vertical strides in a fierce sprint-sell posture - the path must look identical to a go route to freeze the defender's feet and leverage. On the second step, subtly drop the hips an inch into a compact athletic posture while the feet keep moving at full velocity.

representative_fault: BLIND PLANT - the toe points straight ahead or wide of the new path, so the foot brakes instead of steering and the receiver slips off the anchor. Toe left down (plantarflexed) rather than pulled up, so the receiver slides through the plant or stubs the toe instead of biting the ground heel-first. Over-extending or lunging the plant step out ahead of the centre of mass, which costs body control and tips the break early by showing the defender the receiver is gathering rather than still running.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The outside foot lands with the toe pointing exactly down the new route angle, acting as a steering mechanism rather than just a brake. The toe is pulled up into dorsiflexion so the heel bites the grass first, giving clean, firm contact instead of a slide or a stubbed toe. The step stays compact and lands directly beneath the centre of mass - no over-extending or lunging - which both preserves body control and keeps the defender believing the receiver is still accelerating vertically until the instant the weight drops.

representative_fault: BLIND TURN - the torso rotates before the eyes do, so the receiver comes out of the break without having found the ball and is late reacting to a throw already in the air. (Gaze itself is not pose-measurable - orientation only.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The head snaps immediately and fast toward the new route, leading the movement so the eyes find the quarterback before the body has finished turning.

representative_fault: BLIND TURNING - head yaw lagging behind the hip and shoulder rotation, meaning the receiver is turning blind rather than leading with his eyes, and will be late seeing the ball. (Gaze itself is not pose-measurable - orientation only.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The head snaps hard and fast toward the new route trajectory, leading the whole movement - the eyes get there first and the body follows.

representative_fault: BUBBLING THE ROUTE - letting the route angle backward toward the line of scrimmage or bubble downfield. The line must stay flat and parallel to the line of scrimmage to maximise the open void. (Ball location needs ball tracking.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Push violently off the inside instep of the directing foot, sprint flat along the line across the formation, snap the eyes back over the inside shoulder to look for the ball, and secure the catch while bracing to turn upfield.

representative_fault: Chopping or stutter-stepping into the load, which turns a speed cut into a visible breakdown.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Gather into the break with a single subtle hip drop, without chopping or stutter-stepping into the load.

representative_fault: DRIFTING DOWNHILL - allowing the route to angle backward toward the line of scrimmage. The line must stay flat and parallel to the line of scrimmage to keep outrunning the trailing defender.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Push violently off the inside instep of the directing foot, flip the hips wide open, and punch the outside arm across the body to accelerate flat along the 90-degree line toward the sideline.

representative_fault: DRIFTING DOWNHILL - allowing the route to angle backward toward the line of scrimmage. The line must stay flat and parallel to the line of scrimmage to maximise the open void. (Ball location needs ball tracking.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Push violently off the inside instep of the directing foot, sprint flat along the line toward the boundary, snap the eyes back over the inside shoulder to look for the ball, and secure the catch while bracing to turn upfield.

representative_fault: EARLY HANDS - running with the hands extended upward for several yards waiting for the ball. This is a clear signal to the defender, letting them play the arms and break up the pass. (Ball arrival timing needs ball tracking.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Keep the hands down and running until the absolute last moment so the defender is not tipped off to the ball's arrival, then shoot the arms out late, secure the catch away from the frame, and protect the ball.

representative_fault: EXPOSING THE BALL - catching with the body loose or waiting for the ball to hit the chest. Over the middle, failing to snatch with extended hands and instantly tuck results in drops and forced fumbles. (Ball position and contact are not pose-measurable.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Expect a heavy hit from a closing safety or linebacker over the middle. Keep the hands down late to mask the ball's arrival, then shoot the arms up violently to snap the ball out of the air at its highest point, instantly tucking it to protect against incoming contact.

representative_fault: FADING EARLY - drifting inward toward the middle of the field right off the snap. This tells the defender exactly where the receiver is going and lets them squeeze him into the linebacker level. (Absolute depth needs a scale reference.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Explode vertically off the line for 2 to 3 hard steps, driving the pads forward to threaten the defender's leverage and make them respect the go route. Then prepare to redirect sideways by subtly sinking the hips, keeping the feet moving at full speed with no choppy or gathering steps.

representative_fault: FADING EARLY - unconsciously drifting outward toward the sideline before the break depth, alerting the defender to clamp down on the corner. (Absolute depth needs a scale reference and the called depth.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Drive off the line at full velocity for 10-12 yards (12-15 on the deeper variation) with pads leaning forward and long natural strides, pushing the defender into a deep vertical retreat. One step before the break, subtly drop the hips an inch to gather balance and prepare the core for high-speed redirection - without chopping or stutter-stepping.

representative_fault: FADING EARLY - unconsciously drifting outward toward the sideline right off the snap. This tells the defender exactly where the receiver is going and lets them squeeze him into the boundary. (Absolute depth needs a scale reference.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Explode vertically off the line for 2 to 3 hard steps, driving the pads forward to threaten the defender's leverage and make them respect a vertical release. Then prepare to redirect sideways by subtly sinking the hips, keeping the feet moving at full speed with no choppy or gathering steps.

representative_fault: Feet drifting off the stem line during the bait, so the lower body commits before the plant and the cut loses its sharpness.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The feet keep tracking straight under the body along the stem while the upper body begins to turn - the lower body has not yet committed to the break.

representative_fault: FLATTENING THE ANGLE - letting the route angle flat toward the sideline rather than holding a strict 45 degrees toward the corner pylon, which shortens the route and lets the defender close.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Push violently off the inside instep of the directing foot, flip the hips wide open, and punch the outside arm across the body to accelerate along a strict 45-degree line toward the corner.

representative_fault: FLATTENING THE ROUTE - letting the route drift flat toward the opposite sideline instead of holding a true 45-degree angle toward the goal post, which takes the receiver out of the intended throwing window.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Drive powerfully off the inside instep of the directing foot, snap the hips wide open, and punch the outside arm across the body to accelerate down the 45-degree track, holding a low, aggressive acceleration posture.

representative_fault: Hands dropping or going wide during the pause, so the receiver is neither ready for a quick throw nor compact enough to turn fast. (Finger and grip detail needs the Hand landmarker.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The hands stay elevated and active in a compact frame through the pause, ready to catch and tight enough not to slow the rotation.

representative_fault: Head beginning to turn during the load step rather than at the transition, breaking the deception one step too early. (Gaze itself is not pose-measurable - orientation only.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Vision stays fixed downfield right through the load step, holding the deep threat until the exact frame the transition begins.

representative_fault: Head coming round late or after the body has pivoted, so the receiver finishes the break without having found the quarterback - and a ball already in the air arrives before he is looking for it. (Gaze and ball location are not pose-measurable.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The millisecond forward momentum halts, snap the head and eyes back around over the inside shoulder to face the quarterback first. Turning the vision inside opens the upper torso and picks up the ball's trajectory before the lower body has finished its pivot.

representative_fault: Head snap arriving before or after cleat impact rather than with it - either the receiver tips the break early, or he is still turning when the ball is already on its way.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The head snap lands on exactly the same instant as the cleat hits the ground - eyes and anchor arriving together, so the receiver is looking at the quarterback the moment he is able to catch.

representative_fault: Head still rotating at the plant rather than already locked on the new corridor, so the receiver comes out of the cut late to find the ball. (Gaze and ball location are not pose-measurable.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: By the plant the head is fully locked down the new route corridor, already looking for open space and the football before the body has finished turning.

representative_fault: Head turning at the same time as the plant or after it, so the body commits before the eyes have opened the boundary - the torso does not pre-rotate and the break is slower. (Gaze itself is not pose-measurable - orientation only.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: At the exact peak of deceleration, snap the head and eyes sharply toward the sideline first. The visual turn shifts equilibrium and opens the upper torso toward the boundary before the feet leave the turf.

representative_fault: Head turning during the breakdown rather than at the visual snap, giving the defender an extra beat of warning before the break. (Gaze itself is not pose-measurable - orientation only.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Vision stays locked downfield through the breakdown steps, holding the deep threat even as the body gathers to stop.

representative_fault: Head turning so far to track the ball that the body follows and drifts off the route line, or losing the target entirely coming out of the break. (Gaze and ball location are not pose-measurable.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The head tracks the target while staying aligned with the new running lane - the receiver finds the ball without letting his body drift off the route line.

representative_fault: Head turning toward the break direction during the stem, tipping the route before the receiver has reached the break point. (Gaze itself is not pose-measurable - orientation only.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The head stays locked straight downfield through the stem, selling the vertical route and giving the defender nothing to read.

representative_fault: Head turning toward the break during the stem, breaking the vertical threat before the receiver has reached the break point. (Gaze itself is not pose-measurable - orientation only.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Vision stays locked straight downfield through the stem, maintaining the deep vertical threat that makes the stop work.

representative_fault: Head turning with or after the plant rather than leading it, so the receiver breaks across the defender's face without having cleared his vision - and on a route this quick, the ball is often already out. (Gaze and defender positions are not pose-measurable.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: At the exact peak of the third stride, snap the head and eyes inside across the middle of the field first. The visual snap instantly clears vision to read the inside linebackers and pick up the ball's release.

representative_fault: Head turning with or after the plant rather than leading it, so the receiver breaks into the middle without having cleared his vision for crashing inside defenders. (Gaze and defender positions are not pose-measurable.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: At the absolute peak of the breakdown, snap the head and eyes around to face the quarterback first. The visual snap opens the torso and clears vision to read the inside linebackers before the body commits.

representative_fault: Head turning with the plant or after it rather than leading it, so the receiver breaks inside without having read the safety rotation and the torso never pre-rotates. (Gaze and safety position are not pose-measurable.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: At the peak of the stem, snap the head and eyes around to face the near goal post first. The visual snap opens the torso and clears vision to read the safety rotation before the body commits.

representative_fault: Head turning with the plant or after it rather than leading it, so the shoulders never uncoil into the lane and the break is slower than a quick-game route can afford. (Gaze itself is not pose-measurable - orientation only.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: At break depth, snap the head and eyes sharply toward the sideline first. The visual focus locks onto the boundary line, which naturally uncoils the neck and shoulders into the flat lane.

representative_fault: Head turning with the plant or after it rather than leading it, so the shoulders never uncoil into the lane and the receiver crosses without having seen the linebacker level. (Gaze and defender positions are not pose-measurable.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: At break depth, snap the head and eyes sharply across the formation first. The visual focus locks onto the open grass underneath the linebackers, which naturally uncoils the neck and shoulders into the cross lane.

representative_fault: Head turning with the plant or after it rather than leading it, so the torso never pre-rotates and the break is slower and squarer than it should be. (Gaze itself is not pose-measurable - orientation only.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: At break depth, snap the head and eyes sharply toward the corner pylon first. The rapid visual rotation opens the upper torso and shifts equilibrium toward the outside before the lower body begins to pivot.

representative_fault: Hips already rising at the plant rather than bottoming out, so the anchor is weak and the receiver gets carried past the break point.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The hips reach their lowest point of the entire cut at the plant - the core locked down against the ground, giving the anchor maximum stability.

representative_fault: Hips opening to a different angle than the head and plant foot, so the body fights itself through the cut and the exit line is wrong.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The hips snap open to exactly the angle the head and the plant foot have already established - head, foot and hips all pointing down the same new route line.

representative_fault: Hips rising during the pause, unloading the legs - the receiver then has to drop again before he can drive out, and the break is late.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The hips hold their low position through the pause, staying loaded so the plant can fire without needing to re-sink.

representative_fault: Hips rotating fully before the plant, committing early and letting the defender break on the route; or not uncoiling at all, so the plant has to do all the work and the cut rounds off.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The hips begin to uncoil toward the break direction, starting the rotation that the plant will complete.

representative_fault: Knee drive dropping off during the stem, slowing the receiver early and removing the vertical threat the stop cut depends on.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The knees drive at full sprint height through the stem, generating the maximum speed that the breakdown will then have to absorb.

representative_fault: Knee lift dropping off during the stem, which slows the receiver and signals that he is preparing to break rather than running deep.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The front knee lifts high through the swing phase on every stride, sustaining genuine top-end speed down the stem.

representative_fault: Knees extending during the bait, so the receiver arrives at the plant unloaded and cannot absorb the lateral force - the cut slips or rounds.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Both knees stay actively bent through the bait, loaded and ready to handle the high-speed lateral shift that the plant is about to demand.

representative_fault: Knees extending during the pause, so the stored energy leaks away and the drive out has to be generated from scratch.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The deep knee bend is maintained through the pause, keeping the lower body loaded like a spring ready to fire on the plant.

representative_fault: Knees staying relatively straight through the breakdown, so there is nothing to absorb the momentum - the receiver skids, stumbles, or needs extra steps to stop.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Both knees move from maximum sprint drive into deep bilateral flexion, working as shock absorbers to soak up the speed the stem built.

representative_fault: Lead knee staying stiff through the load step, so the sink cannot be absorbed and the receiver either pops up or loses balance going into the plant.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The lead knee bends more deeply on the load step, absorbing the downward force of the sink while keeping the receiver stable at full speed.

representative_fault: LOOKING BACK EARLY - turning the head to look for the ball while it is still in the air and outside the catch radius. Looking back early kills top-end speed and tells the defender to play the hands. (Defender position and stack are not pose-measurable.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Running neck-and-neck with the defender, use a high-speed hand swipe or arm bar to clear their trailing reach, working to stack the body directly in front of their path and strip away their recovery angle - while the head stays locked downfield.

representative_fault: Losing the quarterback coming out of the break, or turning the head so far that the body follows and the exit line curves off the route. (Gaze and ball location are not pose-measurable.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Vision stays locked on the quarterback through the drive out, tracking the throw while the body holds its line on the new trajectory.

representative_fault: Low knee drive out of the break, so the receiver shuffles back up to speed and the throwing window closes before he can separate.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The lead knee drives immediately up and forward out of the plant, converting the stored energy into instant acceleration on the new line.

representative_fault: Low knee drive out of the break, so the receiver shuffles back up to speed and the window the cut opened closes before the ball arrives.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The lead knee drives high and forward out of the cut, generating maximum instant acceleration back to full speed on the new line.

representative_fault: OVERSTRIDING / FLOPPY FOOTWORK - reaching too far forward to try to outrun a deep safety, or running with a loose, downward-pointing toe. This strips core stability and caps top-end speed. Also: drifting laterally out of the void.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Squeeze tightly into the defensive void with the running track completely straight. Steps stay compact and directly beneath the centre of mass without overstriding, toes pulling up into sharp dorsiflexion on every stride for a rigid ankle lock, while the eyes track the ball over the inside shoulder.

representative_fault: OVERSTRIDING / FLOPPY FOOTWORK - reaching too far forward to try to run faster, or running with a loose, downward-pointing toe. This strips core stability, caps top-end speed, and costs balance down the sideline.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The running stride stays completely natural and uninterrupted, steps landing compact and directly beneath the centre of mass without overstriding. The toes pull up into sharp dorsiflexion on every stride to hold a rigid, explosive ankle lock against the turf while the eyes track the ball over the shoulder.

representative_fault: OVERSTRIDING THE BREAK - reaching too far inside with a long, diving step. This elongates the body frame, tells the defender exactly when the break is coming, and locks up the hips so the receiver cannot accelerate smoothly out of the cut.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The millisecond the eyes locate the post, drive the OUTSIDE cutting foot down into a compact step tightly aligned within the frame. The toe is pulled upward into dorsiflexion right before contact to establish a firm ankle lock. The cleat slams down directly beneath the hips, instantly pointing the toe at a sharp 45-degree angle toward the post.

representative_fault: OVERSTRIDING THE BREAK - reaching too far inside with a long, diving step. This elongates the body frame, tells the defender exactly when the break is coming, and locks up the hips so the receiver cannot accelerate smoothly out of the cut. Also: THE FLOPPY-FOOT SLIDE - planting with a loose, downward-pointing toe out in front of the chest, lacking the rigidity to anchor a 90-degree turn, so the shoe slides over the grass.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The instant the eyes locate the inside lane, drive the outside cutting foot down into a compact step tightly aligned within the frame. The toe is pulled upward into dorsiflexion right before contact to establish a firm ankle lock. The cleat slams down directly beneath the hips, instantly pointing the toe at a sharp 90-degree angle toward the middle of the field.

representative_fault: Planting on a stiff leg, which cannot absorb the speed or store energy - the receiver either slides through the cut or has to take recovery steps before accelerating.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The plant knee drops into deep flexion at contact, loading the leg as a high-speed spring that will fire the receiver out on the new line.

representative_fault: Planting on a straight or shallow-bent leg, which cannot absorb the remaining momentum - the receiver skids through the break or jars to a stop with nothing stored for the exit.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The planting knee flexes deep at contact, building a powerful stopping platform that absorbs the last of the momentum and stores it for the drive out.

representative_fault: POPPING UP - a sudden upward spike in hip or chest height, destroying the low sprint angle and broadcasting the break. Also: sinking so far that forward velocity drops and the cut becomes a gather.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The hips drop a small, controlled amount to load the cut - without losing any forward speed. The sink is subtle enough that the defender cannot see it coming.

representative_fault: ROUNDING - the exit trajectory curves rather than forming a sharp line, so the defender recovers the ground the stop had won. Usually caused by the hips rotating too slowly out of the plant.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The hips rotate rapidly to sit parallel with the new exit trajectory, locking the receiver onto a sharp straight line out of the break.

representative_fault: ROUNDING THE ANGLE - the pelvis trajectory forms a wide curve instead of a sharp linear exit, giving the defender time and space to recover the separation the cut had created.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The hips travel on a strict straight line along the new route path, exiting the cut at a sharp angle rather than curving out of it.

representative_fault: RUNNING FLAT - flattening the route out horizontally toward the opposite sideline. The receiver must hold a strict 45-degree angle to keep outrunning the trailing defender. (Ball location needs ball tracking.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Roll the body weight smoothly off the directing foot, punch the outside arm violently across the body to hold top sprinting speed, maintain the 45-degree trajectory, and catch the ball cleanly in stride.

representative_fault: RUNNING FLAT / BANANING - letting the route drift downfield toward the defensive backfield instead of holding a flat, razor-sharp 90-degree line across the middle.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Drive powerfully off the inside instep of the directing foot, snap the hips wide open, and punch the outside arm across the body to accelerate flat across the field, holding a low, aggressive acceleration posture.

representative_fault: Shoulders lagging behind the head turn or staying square, so the upper body does not lead the cut and the transition has to be driven entirely by the plant.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The shoulders turn in time with the head, tilting into the new direction so the upper body initiates the cut and blindsides the defender before the feet move.

representative_fault: Shoulders rotating before or without the head, so the body commits blind and the receiver is late picking up the ball out of the break.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The shoulders rotate in behind the head turn, shifting the body's equilibrium toward the new break so the plant can redirect immediately.

representative_fault: Shoulders sitting back behind the plant foot, so the weight is behind the anchor and the receiver slips backward instead of driving out.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The torso leans securely out over the planting toe, keeping the weight stacked over the anchor so the receiver does not slip backward off the plant.

representative_fault: Shoulders starting to rotate toward the break during the load step, an early tell that lets the defender jump the route.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The shoulders stay completely square to the stem and forward over the knees during the load - the upper body reveals nothing while the lower body prepares.

representative_fault: Shoulders staying out over the toes through the breakdown, so momentum carries the chest forward and the receiver cannot stop cleanly or has to take recovery steps.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The forward sprint lean shifts back into a tucked, balanced position with the shoulders inside the knee frame, so the receiver can anchor rather than being carried forward.

representative_fault: Shoulders staying rotated or the torso staying upright after the cut, so the receiver runs out of the break unbalanced and slow to rebuild speed.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The shoulders square up to the new route line and the torso resumes its forward sprinting lean, the body reset into pure acceleration.

representative_fault: Shoulders staying rotated or the torso staying upright and tucked after the break, so the receiver runs out slow and unbalanced on the new line.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The shoulders square up to the new path and the torso resumes its forward sprint lean, the body reset from stopping posture into pure acceleration.

representative_fault: SLOWING DOWN FOR CONTACT - decelerating or stutter-stepping when an inside linebacker tries to reroute or jam. The receiver must sprint through the contact and use the hands to clear without dropping speed. (Defender contact is not pose-measurable.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Pushing through the intermediate zone at 10-12 yards, expect a collision or squeeze from interior linebackers or safeties. Use a high-speed hand swipe, chop or arm bar to clear their contact while holding the vertical line without drifting off-track or losing a step.

representative_fault: Standing up out of the release rather than driving low, or strides failing to expand into top-end sprint mechanics - either way the receiver never reaches the speed the route depends on.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Explode off the ball with a violent, low pad-level release to clear the press defender's hands and establish the vertical track, then transition from acceleration into full top-speed sprint posture - stride lengths opening to maximum expansion with the chin tucked.

representative_fault: Staying upright through the plant, so momentum carries the receiver wide and the cut rounds off; or over-leaning and losing balance out of the break.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The torso tilts sharply inward toward the new route angle at the plant, countering the centrifugal force of the cut and keeping the receiver balanced through the turn.

representative_fault: STIFF LEG - entering the breakdown with the hips still high, so the deceleration is absorbed through the knees rather than the whole lower body. Slower to stop and hard on the joints.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The hips drop drastically on the breakdown steps, dumping the centre of gravity low so the legs can absorb the speed and the body can anchor.

representative_fault: STIFF-LEGGED BRAKING - trying to stop without sinking the hips. The receiver stumbles forward, takes too many recovery steps, and puts dangerous stress on the knees. (Absolute depth needs a scale reference and the declared route.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Explode off the line and sprint at full vertical velocity for 12-15 yards, forcing the defender to turn their hips into a deep, desperate retreat. At break depth, violently sink the hips and chop the cleats rapidly into the turf - the sudden lowering of the centre of gravity is the braking system that halts forward momentum.

representative_fault: Still carrying forward velocity through the pause, so the receiver drifts past the break point and the route depth is wrong; or the base narrowing and losing the platform for the plant.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The wide, low stance holds for a beat as forward velocity reaches zero - the receiver is genuinely stopped, not still drifting.

representative_fault: Stride shortening on the load step, which is a visible gather and tells the defender the break is one step away.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Stride length holds at its full stem value through the load step while the weight quietly prepares to transfer laterally - nothing shortens or gathers.

representative_fault: STUTTER STEPPING - stride length shortening or step frequency rising before the break point, which tells the defender a cut is coming and surrenders the advantage the stem was built to create.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Stride length stays maximal and constant through the vertical stem - the receiver runs at genuine top speed so the deep route is believable right up to the break.

representative_fault: TELEGRAPHING - stride shortening or velocity dropping before the breakdown, which warns the defender the receiver is about to stop and lets them sit on the route.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Stride length stays maximal through the vertical stem, holding genuine top speed so the deep threat forces the defender to turn and run.

representative_fault: TELEGRAPHING THE STOP - slowing down or rising out of the low pad level a couple of yards before the break point, which lets the defender instantly close the cushion. STIFF-LEGGED BRAKING - trying to stop without sinking the hips, causing a stumble, extra recovery steps, and dangerous stress on the knees.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Explode off the ball and sprint at full vertical velocity to roughly 12 yards, holding a low pad level and natural full strides to drive the defender into a deep backpedal. At break depth, violently sink the hips and chop the cleats rapidly into the turf - the sudden lowering of the centre of gravity is the braking system that halts the momentum the longer stem has built.

representative_fault: THE BLIND PLANT - the foot lands still pointing straight downfield instead of along the new path, so the receiver slides outward, loses his base, and the cut becomes a skid rather than a redirect. Toe left down (plantarflexed) rather than pulled up, so the receiver slides through the plant or stubs the toe instead of biting the ground heel-first. Over-extending or lunging the plant step out ahead of the centre of mass, which costs body control and tips the break early.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The outside cutting foot lands with the toe already pointed along the new route path, steering the body into the break rather than braking against it. The toe is pulled up into dorsiflexion so the heel bites the grass first, giving clean, firm contact instead of a slide or a stubbed toe. The step stays compact and lands directly beneath the centre of mass - no over-extending or lunging - which preserves body control and keeps the defender believing the receiver is still running vertically until the instant the weight drops.

representative_fault: THE DEAD GIVEAWAY - slowing the arm pump or raising the chest before reaching break depth, alerting the defender to clamp down on the out route. (Absolute depth needs a scale reference and the declared route.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Drive off the line at full velocity for 10-12 yards with pads leaning forward and natural full strides, forcing the defender into an aggressive backpedal for fear of the go route. Two steps before break depth, violently sink the hips and chop the cleats to control speed - without standing up or slowing the arm pump.

representative_fault: THE DOWNFIELD TOE PLANT - planting with the toe still pointing toward the end zone. Failing to direct the foot at 90 degrees causes the receiver to drift downfield, running straight into the waiting linebackers.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The instant the eyes find the cross lane, drive the outside foot down into a sharp, compact step positioned firmly beneath the body weight. The toe is pulled up before the foot strikes to ground cleanly. Instantly point the toe and direct the final step down a flat 90-degree track across the field, masking the horizontal break until the last possible instant.

representative_fault: THE FLOPPY-FOOT SLIDE - planting with a loose, downward-pointing toe far out in front of the chest. This lacks the rigidity required to anchor a 90-degree turn, so the shoe slides over the grass and the defender closes the gap.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The instant the eyes find the sideline, drive the INSIDE foot down into a sharp, compact step positioned firmly beneath the body weight. The toe is pulled up into dorsiflexion before the foot strikes to ground cleanly. Instantly point the toe and direct the final step down a flat 90-degree track toward the boundary, masking the horizontal break until the last possible instant.

representative_fault: THE LUNGING SLIDE - lunging too far forward with a loose, downward-pointing toe. The over-extension lacks the rigidity to anchor a 45-degree turn, so the shoe slides over the grass and the defender closes the gap.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: As the eyes lock onto the pylon, drive the INSIDE foot down into a tight, compact step directly under the centre of mass. The toe is pulled up sharply into dorsiflexion right before contact, striking with a rigid foot. Instantly point the toe down a 45-degree track toward the corner, masking the break until the last possible instant.

representative_fault: THE LUNGING SLIDE - lunging too far forward with a loose, downward-pointing toe. The over-extension lacks the rigidity to anchor a 90-degree turn, so the shoe slides over the grass and the defender closes the gap.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: As the eyes find the boundary, slam the inside foot down into a tight, compact step directly under the centre of mass. The toe is pulled up sharply into dorsiflexion right before contact, striking with a rigid foot to lock the brakes. Instantly pivot and point the toe down a flat 90-degree track toward the sideline, masking the break until the last possible instant.

representative_fault: THE LUNGING TOE PLANT - reaching too far forward with the planting step and letting the toe point downward before contact. This strips core stability, causes a slide, and tips off the defender early because the running stride visibly changes before the cut.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: As the eyes find the quarterback, drive the outside cutting foot down into a tight, compact step directly under the hips. The toe is pulled up sharply into dorsiflexion right before contact, striking heel and midfoot first to lock the brakes instantly. Pivot and direct the toe at a 45-degree angle back down the stem toward the sideline.

representative_fault: Too many chop steps, or a gradual slow-down rather than a sharp gather - the breakdown takes too long and the defender closes the space before the break.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Stride shortens rapidly into 2 to 3 chop steps, gathering the feet underneath the body to kill momentum in as little ground as possible.

representative_fault: Torso rising toward upright during the stem, an early tell that the receiver is preparing to break down.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The torso holds an aggressive forward sprint lean through the stem, the posture of a receiver running past the defender rather than one preparing to stop.

representative_fault: Torso rising toward upright during the stem, which reads as a receiver preparing to stop rather than one running past the defender.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The torso holds an aggressive forward lean over the toes through the stem, matching what a genuine deep sprint looks like.

representative_fault: Velocity dropping off during the stem, or excessive vertical bounce wasting energy - either way the deep threat is not sold and the defender does not have to respect it.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The hips carry constant high-speed forward travel with minimal vertical bounce - all the energy goes into covering ground down the stem.

representative_fault: Velocity easing off during the stem, so the deep threat is never established and the defender does not have to respect it.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The hips carry constant high-speed travel down the stem with minimal bounce, selling the vertical route before anything changes.

representative_fault: WAITING ON THE BALL - standing still after making the cut. The receiver must actively run back downhill toward the ball to stop a trailing defender undercutting the route for an interception. (Ball position and defender leverage are not pose-measurable.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Drive powerfully off the inside instep of the directing foot and work back downhill toward the ball, shortening the distance of the throw, squaring the shoulders to the quarterback to shield the ball, and securing the catch with the hands extended away from the frame.

representative_fault: Base too narrow to balance, or so wide it restricts the first step and forces a false step to recover.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Feet are approximately shoulder width apart, providing a stable and explosive base. The stance is wide enough for balance without restricting the first step.

representative_fault: Front knee locked or straight, knee collapsing inside or outside the toe line, or rear knee too extended to contribute to the first movement.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Front knee is bent rather than locked. The knee tracks forward toward the toe while maintaining an athletic loaded position. Rear knee remains flexed enough to contribute to the first movement.

representative_fault: Hands crossed over the body's midline, clamped tight to the torso, or held so low or high that the receiver cannot react to a press. Arms rigid rather than relaxed. (Finger and grip detail needs the Hand landmarker.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Hands remain relaxed, uncrossed, and independent. Hands are positioned near the waist or slightly higher in front of the chest depending on anticipated coverage. Hands remain free to immediately react to a press defender.

representative_fault: Head facing straight downfield rather than turned inside to the ball, or head unstable/bobbing pre-snap so the receiver reacts late. (Gaze itself is not pose-measurable - orientation only. Ball location needs ball tracking.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Head is turned inside toward the football before the snap, with eyes locked onto the ball. The receiver uses the football's movement as the visual snap cue rather than reacting to the quarterback's verbal cadence. Head position remains controlled and stable so the receiver can explode immediately when the ball is snapped without a false start.

representative_fault: Hips opened toward the release before movement begins, giving away direction, or hips drifting out from under the torso so the drive is weakened.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Hips remain loaded underneath the torso and prepared to drive toward the release. Hips should not be excessively opened before movement begins.

representative_fault: Outside foot forward instead of the inside foot; stagger too deep or too shallow to release cleanly; front toe square or turned outward rather than slightly in; or the inward turn overdone so it pulls the hips inside and opens them before the snap. (Which foot is 'inside' depends on alignment side - not determinable from a solo clip.)
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Inside foot is forward, toward the ball. Feet maintain the appropriate stagger and orientation to allow the receiver to release without a false step. The front foot carries a very slight inward turn - enough to aid the release, but not so much that the turn carries up into the hips and opens them inside. The front foot supports the initial roll-off movement.

representative_fault: Shoulders rotated away from the line before the snap, telegraphing the release direction to the defender, or shoulder line unlevel enough to unbalance the first step.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Shoulders remain controlled and aligned with the intended release position. The upper body should not rotate excessively away from the line before movement begins.

representative_fault: Standing too tall with no forward readiness, or crouching so low the receiver cannot release cleanly. Chest behind or well past the front knee.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Chest and hips are lowered into an athletic position. The shoulders/chest are positioned over the front knee, creating forward readiness without excessive crouching.

representative_fault: Swaying, rocking, or bouncing pre-snap rather than settling into a loaded position; or so rigid and locked that the first movement requires a reset. A false step at the snap is the downstream symptom.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Receiver remains stable but immediately movable. The stance is sufficiently loaded to prevent a false step while allowing explosive movement in the intended release direction.

representative_fault: Torso angle diverging from the shin angle - typically folding forward at the waist with the chest well ahead of the shin line, or standing the torso upright while the shin stays loaded, disconnecting upper and lower body.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Upper body is positioned at approximately the same forward angle as the loaded front shin, creating a connected lower- and upper-body position. Avoid excessive bending at the waist.

representative_fault: Weight sitting back on the rear leg or evenly split, forcing a backward rock or false step before the release.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Approximately 70-80% of body weight is loaded onto the front leg. The rear leg remains available to contribute to the release. The receiver should be able to roll forward off the front foot without rocking backward or taking a false step.

representative_fault: "Lunging from the Dirt". Diving forward at the defender's waist out of the stance, which allows an athletic edge rusher to effortlessly slip the block with a quick swim or club-and-rip move.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Pop up rapidly out of the dirt on the snap, replacing the down hand with an instant lateral or backward step to set the edge.

representative_fault: Bailing the Hips. Turning the toes and opening the hips outward too early, which instantly concedes a soft inside path straight into the B-gap.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Keep the shoulders square and sink the hips, aggressively mirroring the rusher to force them wide and around the pocket's deep arc.

representative_fault: Head Dropping. Dropping the chin to the chest upon contact, which breaks the spine angle, eliminates vision, and causes the tight end to slide right off the defender.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Shoot the hands violently straight up into the armpits and inside frame of the defender, locking out the elbows.

representative_fault: Heel Clicking. Bringing the feet together while trying to kick or slide laterally, destroying balance and leaving the tight end helpless against a heavy bull rush.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Establish a wide, stable low-man leverage base, centering the incoming heavy edge rusher squarely between the knees.

representative_fault: Over-stepping Flat. Taking an initial step that is too wide and flat on a zone play, allowing a quick interior defender to shoot underneath and disrupt the backfield.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Take fast, ground-gaining lateral steps off the snap, leveraging the upright stance to instantly close horizontal distance.

representative_fault: Passive "Catching". Standing frozen in place and letting the defender dictate the physical contact, which compresses the edge of the pocket directly into the quarterback.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Push off the inside foot instantly, using the upright advantage to execute an immediate lateral slide to widen the pocket.

representative_fault: Pop and Stop. Landing a powerful initial punch but immediately stopping all foot movement, which allows the defender to shed the block and make the tackle.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Drive the legs relentlessly, churning the feet to physically displace the edge of the defense and clear the primary running lane.

representative_fault: Waist Bending. Reaching forward for a defender by bending at the waist instead of sinking the hips and bending the knees, resulting in a weak, off-balance block.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Sink the hips and bend the knees during the approach to establish a low, powerful striking angle before contact is made.

representative_fault: "False Stepping". Picking up the lead foot and dropping it in place, or taking a slight step backward with the back foot before moving forward, which delays the start of the play.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Push violently off the inside ball of the back foot to initiate explosive forward acceleration.

representative_fault: "Sticking the Hand". Failing to pick up the down hand smoothly, which causes the tight end to lunge forward, lose their footing, and fall to their knees.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Whip the down hand completely off the ground the exact millisecond the foot movement begins.

representative_fault: Standing Straight Up. Raising the head and shoulders on the very first step, which exposes the chest to a defender's jam and eliminates all low-man leverage.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Keep the chin tucked and the chest forward, ensuring the spine angle strictly matches the pre-snap posture without rising.

representative_fault: Tail-Skying. Lifting the hips straight up into the air on the first step instead of driving the hips forward through the block or release.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Explode out of the stance by uncoiling the hips and driving the back foot forcefully into the turf.

representative_fault: "Sticky Contact". Getting physically entangled or staying locked onto the defender for too long, which ruins the timing of the pass play and prevents the tight end from getting open.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: The exact moment the heavy contact lands, seamlessly detach and slip past the defender's outside or inside hip without getting grabbed.

representative_fault: The "Whiff" / Soft Contact. Running past the defender or delivering a weak arm-swipe that fails to disrupt the rusher's track, leaving the offensive tackle out of position.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Deliver a physical, stalling blow directly into the rusher's ribs, shoulder, or chest to violently disrupt their momentum and assist the offensive tackle.

representative_fault: "Standing Tall". Keeping the knees straight and waist unhinged, which raises the pad level and makes the tight end an easy target for defenders to jam or blow off the line of scrimmage.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Hinge at the hips and slightly bend the knees to create a coiled, athletic quarter-squat, rather than standing rigidly straight.

representative_fault: "Tail-Skying" / Too Much Forward Weight. Setting the hips too high or loading too much weight onto the down hand, which causes the tight end to stumble forward or immediately drop their head upon snapping out of the stance.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Sink the hips to establish a low, explosive center of gravity optimized for immediate leverage against heavier defensive ends.

representative_fault: Flat Backside Foot. Letting the heel of the staggered back foot drop completely flat to the turf, which delays the initial forward step and ruins explosive drive.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Stagger the back foot slightly (toe-to-instep or toe-to-heel), keeping the heel elevated to load the calf and Achilles like a coiled spring.

representative_fault: Hands on Thighs. Resting the hands heavily on the thighs pre-snap, which slows down the punch reaction time on a block or delayed release.
representative_ideal_execution_standard: Chamber the hands actively near the waist or chest, keeping them completely unweighted and ready to punch or hand-fight on a release.
